title: [FR] Use --renderToMemory in serve_site()
description:
`hugo server` has changed to write files to disk.

https://gohugo.io/commands/hugo_server/

> The hugo server command will by default write and serve files from disk, but you can render to memory by using the --renderToMemory flag. This can be faster in some cases, but it will consume more memory.

I found this to be frustrating new way of running the server, as I prefer not having files written to disk when running it (I'd just build otherwise).

I'd suggest adding the `--renderToMemory` to the `serve_site()` function.

title: [FR] Set global option for which port serve_site should use
description:
Happy new year Yihui!

Sometimes one needs to always use a specific port when serving a site during local development (e.g. an API might only accepts requests from, say, localhost:3469).

It's possible to serve manually from a specific port with `blogdown::serve_site(port = 3469)`.

However, it's not possible (as far as I could tell) to set a port to use in `.Rprofile`. 

It'd be great if it was possible to set e.g. `options(blogdown.serve_site.port = 3469)` and then whenever serve_site is called, it's serving from that port.

title: Margin along sides of post moving to the right after adding section heading
description:
### Describe the bug

I'm guessing this is related to issue #591. 

When writing a blog post from a rmarkdown file with the introduction theme the margin shifts to the right after adding a section heading.

### Reproduce

- Create site using victoriadrake/hugo-theme-introduction as theme in blogdown in RStudio. Uncheck the options for yaml.
- Go into /content/en/blog and open long_form-post.md. Save that file as a long_form-post-test.Rmd file in the same location.
- Render site

Navigating into blog and then All Posts, you'll see two entries in 2017 for Long Form Writing and Quotes. In the one generated from the .Rmd file, you'll notice the margin shifting after the first section heading. This does not happen in the entry generated from the .md file.

### Expected behavior

The blog entries from the .md and the .Rmd files should produce the same output.

title: 有个疑问：1.9之后的版本为什么不是2.0？
description:
如果之前的版本是1.09，那么1.09之后的版本是1.10就很自然。但是从1.9直接到1.10就感觉不是很自然，因为从数值上判断 1.10 < 1.9，这不利于通过版本号来判断新旧版本，在这方面我想 R 的命名相对更规范点。

建议下一个版本从2.0开始命名。

title: consider deprecating all mentions/recommendations of Google Analytics
description:
* the Danish Data Protection Agency has recently concluded that Google Analytics [cannot be used lawfully](https://www.datatilsynet.dk/english/google-analytics/use-of-google-analytics-for-web-analytics)
* It's reasonable to think that other agencies will follow suit (there's been some [early signs in that direction](https://www.androidpolice.com/google-analytics-gdpr-eu-violation/))
* The Blogdown book doesn't precisely _endorse_ Google Analytics, but does describe it as part of the [default flow](https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/themes.html), which might be _read_ as a soft endorsement
* I recently installed [plausible analytics](https://plausible.io/) [on my own blog](https://github.com/setgree/setharielgreen/commit/adf2ed9e1290263ff286b40f779bf5dc0e75d8c8), and it took a bit of searching around but ultimately was not that hard
* Maybe the blogdown project as a whole should consider removing mentions of Google Analytics from its documentation/default templates and switching over to privacy-focused alternatives instead?


Thanks in advance!

title: Using RStudio addins will kill the hugo server in the background
description:
I upgraded RStudio from 2022.02.3,492 to 2022.07.1,554 yesterday and found that the `hugo server` launched by `blogdown::serve_site()` would almost always be killed after I close any RStudio addin (e.g., the "New Post" addin of **blogdown**). That is, as soon as I close the addin, the website preview is dead. This only happens with `options(blogdown.use.processx = FALSE)` (i.e., the background process is launched via `system2(wait = FALSE)`).

I spent a couple of hours on trying to figure out why this happens but didn't find out the culprit. I thought it was because of the new RStudio version, but even if I go back to the older version, the same thing occurs. Other findings:

1. It's not limited to RStudio addins, but any Shiny apps. If I run and stop any Shiny app, the hugo server is stopped, too.
2. I tested several Hugo versions and only 0.25/0.26 survived. I also tested other background processes (e.g., a shell script with an infinite loop), and they wouldn't be killed.
3. `options(blogdown.use.processx = TRUE)` works fine (the process won't be killed).

I'm not sure if this is specific to macOS. @cderv Are you able to reproduce it on Windows/Linux?

title: Proactively test Hugo themes
description:
From https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/704#issuecomment-1119237429

Originally I was thinking of testing only a few themes in a GHA daily workflow:

```r
themes = c(
  'hugo-apero/hugo-apero',
  'wowchemy/starter-hugo-academic',
  'wowchemy/starter-research-group',
  'yihui/hugo-prose'
)
for (theme in themes) {
  d = tempfile()
  dir.create(d)
  xfun::in_dir(d, {
    blogdown::new_site(theme = theme, serve = FALSE)
    blogdown::build_site(build_rmd = 'newfile')
  })
  unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
}
```

But it may be a better idea to test all themes: https://github.com/gohugoio/hugoThemesSiteBuilder/blob/main/themes.txt and generate a "status" page that shows which themes work or do not work with **blogdown**. This page could be a simple (meaning a plain style) HTML page deployed along with https://pkgs.rstudio.com/blogdown/. We can save the results in the artifacts, and make the pkgdown workflow read and deploy the results.

title: Table of Contents Does Not Work With `blogdown.method = "html"`
description:
I use the [hugo-theme-fuji](https://themes.gohugo.io/themes/hugo-theme-fuji/) theme, but I think this issue has nothing to do with that.
When I had `blogdown.method = "markdown"` in `root/.Rprofile`, the table of contents worked perfectly fine but citations in figure captions didn't work.
So I switched `blogdown.method` to `html`, but this caused the table of contents to not work (There are section headers in all of my blog posts.)

[My website](https://amarakon.github.io/amarakon.com), [source code](https://github.com/amarakon/amarakon.com)

Reproducible example:

1. Create a new website by using `blogdown::new_site()`
2. Use the fuji hugo theme as mentioned above
3. Set `blogdown.method = "html"` in `root/.Rprofile`
4. Create a blog post with section headers

title: [FR] Twitter shortcode is changing syntax: when would it be appropriate to update the docs?
description:
Hi,

Given the changes in Twitter's API, hugo had to change their `shortcode` for it. See https://discourse.gohugo.io/t/the-tweet-shortcode-will-soon-require-two-named-parameters-user-and-id/35871/2 which links to https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/0cc39af68232f1a4981aae2e72cf65da762b5768.

With that in mind, https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/34fd54646b35de50ad68002750fa74e6f93e70ee/docs/02-hugo.Rmd#L202 will likely need to change to `{{< tweet user="jtleek" id="852205086956818432" }}` and https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/34fd54646b35de50ad68002750fa74e6f93e70ee/docs/02-hugo.Rmd#L211 to `blogdown::shortcode('tweet', user='jtleek', id='852205086956818432')`.

Here's an example:


``` r
blogdown::shortcode("tweet", user="lcolladotor", id="983876013015826432")
# {{% tweet user="lcolladotor" id="983876013015826432" %}}
```

<sup>Created on 2022-04-30 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

However, I'm not sure if this will affect users who are using older versions of Hugo. So I'm not sure if changing the documentation makes sense.

In any case, `hugo` will still work with the old shortcodes for a while.

In my personal case, it's a pain since I used this shortcode a lot at https://github.com/lcolladotor/lcolladotorsource:

```
% hugo version
hugo v0.98.0+extended darwin/arm64 BuildDate=unknown
```

title: "404 NOT FOUND" For Blog Posts
description:
<!--
Welcome to the blogdown GitHub repo !

We are always happy to hear feedback from our users. 

To file a _bug report_, please follow these instructions carefully: <https://yihui.org/issue/#bug-reports>

Also, please complete and keep the checklist below in your issue. This helps you know what to check for opening a good issue report. It also helps know that you've have done the common steps that can solve your potential issue.

At last, if you have posted the same issue elsewhere, please mentioned it (with a link to the other issue).

## Checklist

When filing a _bug report_, please check the boxes below to confirm that you have provided us with the information we need. Have you:

- [ ] [formatted your issue](https://yihui.org/issue/#please-format-your-issue-correctly) so it is easier for us to read?

- [ ] used `blogdown::check_site()` function to diagnose your site and corrected potential problems?

- [ ] included a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example?

- [ ] pasted the output from `xfun::session_info('blogdown')` in your issue?

- [ ] upgraded all your packages to their latest versions (including your versions of R, the RStudio IDE, and relevant R packages)?

- [ ] installed and tested your bug with the development version of the blogdown package using `remotes::install_github('rstudio/blogdown')` ?

-->

I have my website source code at https://github.com/Amarakon55/amarakon.com. The website is published through the _docs/_ directory. The website URL is currently https://amarakon55.github.io/amarakon.com. I have a blog post titled "Test Post" which I can view by running `blogdown::serve_site()` to preview the site. However, my actual website can't view the post. [Try it.](https://amarakon55.github.io/amarakon.com/post/2022-04-30-test-post/) It is also built fine so that is not the issue.

Here is the output of `xfun::session_info('blogdown')`:

```
> xfun::session_info('blogdown')
R version 4.1.2 (2021-11-01)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Gentoo Linux

title: [FR]: Add support for `bundle exec jekyll`
description:
Jekyll sites are supported via `options(blogdown.generator = "jekyll")`.
Yet some sites make use of `bundler`, which is similar to {renv} in that it runs on a lockfile which defines the gem versions.

Often enough a normal call to `jekyll` won't work for such environments.
Hence one would need to call `bundle exec jekyll` to make `blogdown::serve_site()` work.
Currently this is not supported.

Adding support for `bundle exec jekyll` would be great! (PR incoming)

title: New post writes incorrect yaml if archetype contains yaml unnamed list
description:
Take this `test.Rmd` file 
```markdown
---
links:
  - icon: images
    icon_pack: fas
    name: slides
    url:
  - icon: github
    icon_pack: fab
    name: code
    url:
---

Content

```

`new_post()` will at some point try to modify the YAML header, and this is where we loose the correct YAML format: 

``` r
save_copy <- file.copy("test.Rmd", "test.Rmd.save")
xfun::file_string("test.Rmd")
#> ---
#> links:
#>   - icon: images
#>     icon_pack: fas
#>     name: slides
#>     url:
#>   - icon: github
#>     icon_pack: fab
#>     name: code
#>     url:
#> ---
#> 
#> Content
blogdown:::modify_yaml("test.Rmd")
xfun::file_string("test.Rmd")
#> ---
#> links:
#>   icon: images
#>   icon_pack: fas
#>   name: slides
#>   url: ~
#>   icon: github
#>   icon_pack: fab
#>   name: code
#>   url: ~
#> ---
#> 
#> Content
rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("test.Rmd")
#> Error in yaml::yaml.load(..., eval.expr = TRUE): Duplicate map key: 'icon'


# restore
file.rename("test.Rmd.save", "test.Rmd")
#> [1] TRUE
```


All the `-` in front of the YAML list item are removed which leads to incorrect YAML. 

_First reported in https://community.rstudio.com/t/having-nested-elements-on-blogdown-hugo-archetypes/127761/2 by @llrs_

title: [FR] config option for multiple custom rendering functions
description:
Hi all,

(This is an edited repost from #289 which hasn't received a response in 6 months. If it's on people's radar, please feel free to close this issue)

A tiny bit of background: I am a uni teacher so hosting both slides and lecture handouts/worksheets in an integrated easy-to-use, easy-to-maintain way is important when creating a course website.
I think that enabling users to define custom formats while keeping `blogdown::html_page` as the default should be fairly simple.

Here is my suggestion (implemented [in this commit](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/commit/a44ff2bd0bac506b7aa78faf6cdfa64929642234)):
`config.yaml` should have an optional renders: parameter, such as:

```
renders:
  default: "blogdown::html_page"
  slides: "my_pkg::my_format"
```

`blogdown::build_site()` then reads renders from `config.yaml` and passes it down to `blogdown:::build_one()` which looks for the type: parameter in a .Rmd file's YAML front matter. If there isn't one, the file gets rendered by the default method. In this scenario, files with `type: slides` in YAML get rendered with `my_pkg::my_format`.
Using the `type: param` is handy because it allows custom HUGO templates for files of a given type.

If there is no `renders:` in `config.yaml`, everything gets rendered by `blogdown::html_page` so it would not be a breaking change.

The implementation linked above doesn't deal with TOML but I don't imagine it would take a lot of work to expand.
I've been working on a blogdown/HUGO theme for course websites I would like to release and this feature is crucial for it.

Many thanks!

title: How to use Netlify identity widget in R blogdown
Unable to access .GitInfo from template when knitting Rmd file
description:
Hi!

I have a working `{blogdown}` site which works wonderfully. I'm wanting to enhance one of the templates to use the `.GitInfo` structure. I've got some old posts that are in `.md` files and most of the newer posts are in `.Rmd` files.

With the old `.md` files the rendered post contains the expected values from `.GitInfo`.

However, with the `.Rmd` files the rendered post simply contains `<nil>` where I expect to see `.GitInfo`.

I have a hypothesis for why this happens:

- the `.md` files exist in the Git repository and so Hugo is able to extract the corresponding information from Git; but
- the only the `.Rmd` files exist in the Git repository (and not the interim `.md` files which I understand are being generated by knitting the `.Rmd` files and that are then being processed by Hugo). Since Hugo can't find the `.md` file (and doesn't know to look for a `.Rmd` file) the `.GitInfo` structure doesn't get populated.

Does that sound feasible? And, if so, is there a way to work around this?

My first objective with doing this is to have an "updated" timestamp on each post which will be derived from the latest commit relevant to a file. However, I have other ideas for how this Git information could be used too.

Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Best regards, Andrew.

title: Consider setting `HUGO_CACHEDIR` to use the tmpdir of the R session?
description:
Recent versions of hugo use `/tmp/hugo_cache` as a cache file location, which is badly suited to multi-tenant systems and will throw permission errors such as:

```
Error: add site dependencies: create deps: failed to create file caches from configuration: mkdir /tmp/hugo_cache/filea68f64c4f01c0: permission denied
```

See  https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/7391 for details.  

Hopefully this will be fixed upstream in hugo, but meanwhile, `blogdown` (or the end user) could avert the problem by setting the environmental variable `HUGO_CACHEDIR` to a more appropriate path.  

For instance, as you know, R uses a subdir within `/tmp` as `tempdir()`, which is very reasonable as it avoids permission issues and allows R to purge tmp files between sessions.  Alternately this could be set to the OS-specific user cache dir, as provided by `rappdirs`/`tools`.  Not sure which is better, but either would be preferable to writing directly to `/tmp/hugo_cache`, which seems to go against long-standing conventions for appropriate caching.  (Notably, using the R-set `tempdir()` would case the cache to be purged between R sessions; perhaps that's not desirable in this case, so the application-specific destination is probably correct.

I recognize this is fundamentally a hugo issue, so feel free to close, but as most of us look first to blogdown so maybe this will at least be a pointer to anyone hitting this error.

title: academic
[FR] Ability to set default print method for all posts
description:
First of all, a huge thank you to package author and maintainers - blogdown is an amazing package to work with. 

A common request from our users is the ability to render data frames and tibbles in a better way than the default print method in blogdown, e.g. using `rmarkdown::paged_table()` or `DT::datatable()`. We were able to switch the default method of a post by adding the following chunk from the `knit_print`-[vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/knitr/vignettes/knit_print.html): 

``````r
---
title: "Print Issue"
---

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# Set default print method for data.frames
library(knitr)
knit_print.data.frame = function(x, ...) {
  knitr::knit_print(rmarkdown:::print.paged_df(x), ...)
}
registerS3method("knit_print", "data.frame", knit_print.data.frame, envir = globalenv())
```

# Prints paged table
```{r cars}
cars
```

``````
Which works great:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16469189/136713084-a0cf7fc0-48b0-4bcb-8c74-15004b634919.png)

It's not obvious to users that they would need to copy this chunk to a new post to achieve better printing, so we wanted to set it as the default for all posts. Our first thought was to move the `knit_print`-chunk above to `.Rprofile`, but that reverted back to the old print method for data frames:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16469189/136713013-ef0e271c-d531-4b0e-9a07-cb2ced50846b.png)

We suspect that this may be because the rendering process of blogdown overrides it, but we have not been able to figure out exactly how.  Using `paged.print=TRUE` could be a good workaround for our us, but it does not seem to have any effect on the output in the current version.

I have not been able to locate any other documentation related to default print methods in blogdown, so I thought this could be a useful addition for others.  Apologies if there's something we have overlooked. 

Thanks again for your amazing work!

title: Using `docs` subdirectory to publish to gh-pages

The blogdown book states there are two ways to deploy to github pages.

https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/e40271a5417c9e1788d3e926dc3479badc791c73/docs/03-deploy.Rmd#L73

Either make the publish directory the repository for username.github.io or have a source directory.

I think that the following is preferable to both, and should be suggested as the main option (if using gh-pages) in the book:
Have the complete repo called username.github.io
Publish to a subdirectory called `docs`.
Add the .nojekyll file to `docs`.
Setup under settings->pages->Branch: main /docs

title: Automatically add tags based on library calls in post [FR]
description:
Would be nice if had easy way to set tags based on the library calls used in that post. Something like:

``` r
library(stringr)
library(magrittr)

tag_libs <- function(file_path, include_explicit = TRUE){
  
  file <- readr::read_lines(file_path)
  
  lib_calls <- str_extract_all(file, "(?<=library\\().+(?=\\))", simplify = TRUE)
  
  if(include_explicit){
    explicit_calls <- str_extract_all(file, "[[:alnum:]|\\.]+(?=::)", simplify = TRUE)
  } else {
    explicit_calls <- NULL
  }
  
  str_remove_all(lib_calls, '"') %>% 
    c(explicit_calls) %>% 
    str_subset(pattern = ".+") %>%
    sort() %>% 
    unique() %>% 
    str_flatten("\n  - ") %>% 
    str_c("  - ", .) %>% 
    cat()
}

# Example from one of my blogs
file_path <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brshallo/brshallo/master/content/post/2021-03-18-intuition-on-uncertainty-of-predictions-introduction-to-prediction-intervals.html"

tag_libs(file_path)
#>   - AmesHousing
#>   - forcats
#>   - ggplot2
#>   - gt
#>   - pander
#>   - parsnip
#>   - scales
#>   - tidymodels
#>   - tidyverse
#>   - workflows
#>   - yardstick
```

<sup>Created on 2021-08-10 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

Ideally set-up so may run without hassle of typing out `filepath`. For example could...

* be selected via an option when calling the "Update Metadata" or other add-in function.
* set in the YAML as an option under "tags" or under "output" --> "blogdown::html_page".

## Motivation

I can relate to @yihui comment https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/172#issuecomment-319569278

> Personally I don't even use categories or tags in my blogs since I'm lazy and I don't think my blogs are so big and complicated that I need taxonomies to manage them.

The tags I've self-set on posts have mostly ended-up being useless or essentially duplicates of my Category labels. I thought the option to use the library's called within a post would be a more natural way of setting/navigating tags on my rstats posts.

install_hugo() on ARM chips
description:
Hi, 

When I use ` blogdown::install_hugo()` on a machine with an ARM processor, it tries to install the x64 version and fails. I downloaded the ARM version from Hugo's release page and followed @yihui 's answer [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61317355/error-installing-hugo-using-blogdownhugo-install) to install Hugo on my Ubuntu 20.04 machine, but it failed. It didn't show me the exact error, but `blogdown::check_hugo()` told me that Hugo was not installed.

The Hugo version on the apt store is old, so using the version from `apt install hugo` won't help while building a site. I had to download the required version of Hugo from GitHub and install it manually using the Ubuntu terminal. It'll be great if you can add support for ARM-based machines since the base R has been ported to support ARM chips.

title: Simultaneous TOC and inline maths
description:
There are (at least) two things that I would like for my blog post pages to have:

1. _a table of contents_; and
2. _inline maths rendering_.

If I use `.Rmarkdown` files, then the first one is easy (using Hugo's `{{ .TableOfContents }}`), but inline maths rendering doesn't work (and I can't get the JavaScript fix described in §B.3 of the manual to work, but that might be because I'm using KaTeX instead of MathJax).

If I use `.Rmd` files, then the second one works just fine, and the first one _sort of_ works (by using `toc: true` in `blogdown::html_page:`), but the outputted table of contents is a `<ul>` instead of a `<nav>`, and also shows up when I use `{{ .Summary }}` to display a short version of the blog post. For some reason, with `.Rmd` files, the Hugo `{{ .TableOfContents }}` no longer works.

My dream solution would involve finding a way to use Hugo's table of contents instead of the `blogdown::html_page`-generated one so that I could continue to use `.Rmd` files, which work beautifully with KaTeX, but I'd also be happy with the opposite solution, namely fixing inline maths rendering (**without** asking the user to wrap everything in code blocks) so that I could use `.Rmarkdown` files.

Please let me know if I can provide any more information!

title: md5sum_filter changed without notice
description:
Raising this since I didn't see it mentioned anywhere else:

A while back I added some options to my .Rprofile in my blogdown site based on recommendations from @apreshill in a workshop, which included the following:
```
options(blogdown.hugo.version = "0.79.0", # fix Hugo version
        blogdown.knit.on_save = FALSE, 
        blogdown.files_filter = blogdown:::md5sum_filter,  # fixes date issues
        # other nice to haves!
        blogdown.title_case = TRUE,
        blogdown.initial_files = FALSE,
        # nice defaults!
        blogdown.new_bundle = TRUE,
        blogdown.warn.future = TRUE,
        blogdown.draft.output = FALSE)
```

When I went to render my website today, I kept getting the following error:
```
Error in options(blogdown.hugo.version = "0.79.0", blogdown.knit.on_save = FALSE,  : 
  object 'md5sum_filter' not found
```

In the intervening months, it seems that `md5sum_filter` changed to now be `filter_md5sum`. This will likely be an issue for anyone who was calling on that old internal function and since it took me a while to figure out what was going on (hard to find anything on it as it's not an exported function!) I thought it was worth posting here.

title: Update the book
description:
I'm using this issue to flush out some things I'd like to update in the blogdown book: ## Get started 1. Installation (updated in #618) 2. A quick example (updated in #618) [notes: no GitHub, `hugo-lithium` theme, no deploy, edit post only] 3. A quick deploy (added in #619) [notes: still no GitHub, `hugo-lithium` theme, Netlify Drop] 4. A complete example (draft in #623) [notes: GitHub, wowchemy theme, edit + add new post, Netlify continuous deployment] 5. Other themes (updated in #620) 6. Recommended workflows (will need an update after all of the above, idea is more like a cheatsheet/tl;dr version of above content, will include GitHub) ## The blogdown package Propose a new chapter with these sections: 1. RStudio Addins (adapt from https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/rstudio-ide.html) 2. Using R Markdown (adapt from https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/output-format.html, plus add https://blog.rstudio.com/2021/01/18/blogdown-v1.0/#better-support-for-markdown-format) 3. Global options (adapt from https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/global-options.html; be sure to mention all of [these](https://twitter.com/DrMowinckels/status/1375550447407276037?s=20)) 4. Checking functions (adapt from https://blog.rstudio.com/2021/01/18/blogdown-v1.0/#checking-functions) 5. Hugo versioning system (adapt from https://blog.rstudio.com/2021/01/18/blogdown-v1.0/#hugo-versioning-system) WIP draft chapter in branch here: https://github.com/apreshill/blogdown/blob/blogdown-chapter/docs/02-blogdown.Rmd
Some rationale

Help users realize what blogdown actually does, vs Hugo/GitHub/Netlify. Folks often ask this in workshops and meetups, and with the checking functions and versioning system, I think the package now deserves its own chapter to highlight how we make using Hugo in the RStudio IDE easier.

title: Quotes become U+201C in HTML generated files
description:
I use blogdown to generate a website with some custom shortcodes to generate some nice boxes. 

You can find an example at the bottom of the page [there](https://linogaliana-teaching.netlify.app/git/introgit/) which is based on a shortcode [here](https://github.com/linogaliana/hugo-theme-techdoc/blob/fe335552659b86640934a14672ba547b6c69931b/layouts/shortcodes/panel.html) that is called like that in a Rmd file (sorry  English speaking people, that's a copy-paste of French content but the text does not matter) :

```r
{{% panel status="tip" title="Tip" icon="fa fa-lightbulb" %}}
`Git` a été conçu, initialement pour la ligne de commande. Il existe
néanmoins des interfaces graphiques performantes
et pratiques, notamment lorsqu'on désire comparer deux versions d'un même
fichier côte à côte. Ces interfaces graphiques couvrent la majorité des
besoins quotidiens. Néanmoins, pour certaines tâches, il faut nécessairement
passer par la ligne de commande.
{{% /panel %}}
```

Up to now, I was knitting the files in local to get the `.md` and committing directly the `.md` file, letting GHA actions build the website from `.md`. I am trying to improve my continuous integration setup by only committing the `.Rmd` file and stop committing the `.md` file. 

This is the point where I noticed a difference.

**I created a MWE [here](https://github.com/linogaliana/blogdown-MWE) to illustrate the problem**. This is the basic blogdown project with an additional shortcode that is used in [this file](https://github.com/linogaliana/blogdown-MWE/blob/master/content/post/2020-12-01-r-rmarkdown/index.Rmd#L40-L47)

When I use `blogdown::build_site(local = TRUE, build_rmd = TRUE)` on the MWE, I end up with the following error:

```r
got positional parameter 'fa-lightbulb'. Cannot mix named and positional parameters
```

It seems weird because I explicitly use named parameters. So I tried removing the names and I got a new error:

```r
unrecognized character in shortcode action: U+201C 'â€œ'. Note: Parameters with non-alphanumeric args must be quoted
```

I looked at the HTML generated by `blogdown:::build_rmds`. I think I found the responsible: `"` becomes `“` (U+201C). This makes hugo fail (because hugo needs quoted named parameters and things between U+201C are not recognized as quoted values).

Is there a way to prevent this `"` -> `“` transformation ?


PS: `blogdown` is a very nice package. As you might have seen, I use it for a `Python` website ! 🐍

title: better hugo version help
description:
From my troubleshooting help diaries-

```
> blogdown::install_hugo()
The latest Hugo version is v0.82.0
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
You have set the option 'blogdown.hugo.version' to '0.82' (perhaps in .Rprofile), but you are installing the Hugo version '0.82.0' now. You may want to update the option 'blogdown.hugo.version' accordingly.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
trying URL 'https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/releases/download/v0.82.0/hugo_extended_0.82.0_macOS-64bit.tar.gz'
Content type 'application/octet-stream' length 15013690 bytes (14.3 MB)
==================================================
downloaded 14.3 MB

Hugo has been installed to "/Users/lowndes/Library/Application Support/Hugo/0.82.0". 
> blogdown:::serve_site()
Error: Hugo 0.82 not found. You may try blogdown::install_hugo("0.82").
```

This person didn't realize that Hugo versions need the trailing dot (so 0.82 is not equal to 0.82.0; [this doesn't help!](https://gohugo.io/news/0.82.0-relnotes/))- can the message that prints be clearer? Suggestion:

```
You have set the option 'blogdown.hugo.version' to '0.82' (perhaps in .Rprofile), but you are installing the Hugo version '0.82.0' now. You may want to update the option 'blogdown.hugo.version' accordingly.
```

Instead to be more actionable: 

```
You are installing Hugo version '0.82.0' now. 
● [TODO] To match your installed version, set `options(blogdown.hugo.version = "0.82.0")` in your .Rprofile.
```

And then maybe `serve_site()` could hint if the Hugo version is >= 0.54.0, that valid Hugo versions include two decimals?

title: support config dir
description:
Hi.

I have a website running well in hugo that wont run with blogdown currently.
its a complex site with multilingual features, so I've opted to use the [hugo config dir](https://gohugo.io/getting-started/configuration/#configuration-directory) rather than a single config file in order to keep the config more tidy. 

The config dir is currently not supported in blogdown, so I wanted to get a feel for if/when y'all would have the time to look at that. 

I guess, the ideal situation would be something that autodetects the config folder (lke hugo does) or an option to specify that config is in a folder rather than a single file. Either of these options would make sense to me. Default would anyway be a single file, since I think 99% of users have simpler setups.

Could it be because `serve_site()` is not correctly finding `postcss`, `postcss-cli` and `autoprefixer` in `PATH`? title: 3.4 gitlab pages improvement
description:
Hi Yihui, Amber & Alison,

I'm not completely sure of myself, but as it worked for me maybe it can help other people.
I changed my `gitlab-ci.yml` from
``` yml
image: rocker/tidyverse

before_script:
  - apt-get update
  - R -e "install.packages(c('blogdown', and_so_on), repos='https://cran.rstudio.com/')"
  - R -e "blogdown::install_hugo()"

pages:
  script:
  - R -e "blogdown::build_site()"
  artifacts:
    paths:
    - public
  only:
  - master
  ```
to the usual hugo one
``` yml
image: monachus/hugo

variables:
  GIT_SUBMODULE_STRATEGY: recursive

pages:
  script:
  - hugo
  artifacts:
    paths:
    - public
  only:
  - master
```
and the deployment time dropped from 30 minutes to **30 seconds**! Tidyverse and the other packages I needed are the longest to load. The new config seems to work for `.rmd` content as well because of their trailing `.html`, so it is a bit of a hack because this was probably not expected by you, developer ;)

Well I was thinking maybe it is worth a while to test the robustness of this config a bit further (I use wowchemy and icon hugo themes but don't have any sophisticated workflow) and let it know to the wide world.

Cheers
Anna

title: Working with renv and blogdown, a few remarks on the current state
description:
At the present, there is nothing stopping us from making each blog post an renv project, but apart from blogdown not actually using the renv environment (#469), there are a few small gotchas.

You really need to add the `renv` directory to your `ignoreFiles` list. Without this, Hugo will traverse the `renv` tree during its site build, and inevitably choke on the first HTML file it encounters there. 
You probably want to add the `renv.lock` file to your `ignoreFiles` list. If we don't Include `renv.lock` in `ignoreFiles` Hugo will publish that file alongside your HTML file, which is usually not desirable.

```
ignoreFiles: 
  - "\\.Rmd$"
  - "\\.Rmarkdown$"
  - "\\.Rproj$"
  - "\\.RData$"
  - "\\.Rhistory$"
  - "\\.Rnw$"
  - "\\.pdf$"
  - "\\.sqlite.*$"
  - "_cache$"
  - "\\.knit\\.md$"
  - "\\.utf8\\.md$"
  - "renv"   # if you're on blogdown v0.21+, don't use any trailing slash!
  - "renv\\.lock$"
```

`blogdown::build_site(...)` now [knows to skip the `renv` tree](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/pull/453) (note that this is hard-coded, and not dependent on your `ignoreFiles`), but `blogdown::check_site()` still peruses the `renv/` tree inside each blog post, which makes it unnecessarily chatty (but does not really break anything), for example:

```
― Checking content files
| Checking for validity of YAML metadata in posts...
● [TODO] Found invalid YAML metadata in the following files:

  content/post/2015-02-07-rod-with-conformal-layer/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/tikzDevice/NEWS.md (Reason: Scanner error: while scanning a simple key at line 4, column 1 could not find expected ':' at line 5, column 1
)

  Please fix the YAML metadata of these files.
[...]
● [TODO] Found 221 incompatible .html files introduced by previous blogdown versions:
### [I am purposely not showing all 221 rows here...]
  file.remove(c(
  "content/post/2014-09-13-xray-line-energies/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/ggplot2/doc/ggplot2-specs.html",
  "content/post/2015-03-20-sem-tiffinfo/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/tibble/doc/formats.html",
  "content/post/2019-01-20-rstudio-server-multiple-instances-kvm/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/knitr/examples/knitr-spin.html",
  "content/post/2020-11-17-measurement-errors/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/units/doc/measurement_units_in_R.html"
  ))

  To fix, run the above command and then blogdown::build_site(build_rmd = "newfile").
```

If you, like me, are interested in using renv together with blogdown, I suggest you start by skimming through issues #451 and #469. Thanks to @cderv [for asking me to collect my thoughts](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/451#issuecomment-783998539) on the subject into one issue. I hope this does not confuse the subject.

title: Margin along sides of post disappear after adding section heading.
description:
**Describe the bug**
Margin along sides of post disappear after adding section heading. I don't think it is the theme, but maybe it is just a problem with the interactions between blogdown and newer version of hugo or markdown flavors.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
- Create site using `CaiJimmy/hugo-theme-stack` as theme in blogdown in RStudio.
- Create new post.
- Add body text.
- Render site/page.
- Then add a section heading in the middle of the post.
- Render site again, at which point the margins disappear.

**Expected behavior**
- I would expect that after a section heading, the body text and images would still have a margin.

**Screenshots**

The body text above the section heading preceding the first heading of the post, but after the section heading, the margins disappear.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
Windows 10
Chrome 88
Hugo 0.81
Latest blogdown version
Latest RStudio version

**Additional context**
Site rendered with blogdown package in RStudio. This behavior is likely not due to the theme choice, as the theme demo page shows posts with margins all the way through even after section headings.

title: Add option to configure site root directory
description:
I am creating a blogdown website for an upcoming workshop. My GitHub repository is structured similar to the [Introduction fo Machine Learning in the Tidyverse](https://github.com/rstudio-conf-2020/intro-to-ml-tidy) repository from rstudio::conf(2020). That is, blogdown source files are in the `site/` sub-directory and other materials for the workshop are in the `materials/` directory. However, when blogdown source files are not in the project working directory, the Serve Site addin fails because it does not know to look in a subdirectory. It would be useful to have an option that could be added to the project's `.Rprofile` that could specify the site root (e.g., `options(blogdown.site_root = "site/")`).

It seems like this could be accomplished by changing the definition of `blogdown::serve_site()` to 

```r
serve_site = function(..., .site_dir = getOption(blogdown.site_root, default = NULL))
```

https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/7399df2637686a98f665520abca2d15fba0d0151/R/serve.R#L41

This would (I think) preserve the current behavior for any user where the the `blogdown.site_root` option is unspecified, but would allow users to specify a different directory if desired.

Following discussion with @cderv on [RStudio Community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/blogdown-serve-site-from-subdirectory/94658) there are a few alternative solutions, all with some drawbacks. The first is use the Knit button in RStudio. This now serves the site; however, this requires you to first have an `.Rmd` or `.Rmarkdown` file open. If you just open the project, or are working on another file (e.g., `config.toml`), the Knit button is not available to you. A second option is to add `setwd("site")` to the `.Rprofile`. This is my current workaround, as it makes the addin work correctly. However, it feels a bit icky to set my working directory to be different from the project directory (and I'm a little afraid Jenny Bryan might come and set my laptop on fire :smile:).

If the proposed solution is acceptable, I'd be happy to submit a PR with this change.

title: knit forcing preview_site
description:
I just updated to the latest blogdown to check out the new features, and for me its having some unexpected effects.

With the newest version I am experiencing in my opinion somewhat aggressive and unwanted blogdown behaviour.
1. manually knitting no longer keeps md as specified in the yaml
2. manually knitting starts `preview_site`

Nr. 1 _just_ found a solution to, but since it was quite hidden I'm going to write it here anyway, in case someone else is struggling with something similar. Since the change in `method` my workaround specifying in the yaml `keep_md: yes` was ignored. After some trial an error I found that setting `options(blogdown.method = "markdown")` in `.Rprofile` now renders md rather than html (which is what I wanted with my workaround, thank you, now I can scrap that!). Adding `blogdown.knit.on_save = FALSE` to the options was also a great relief to me.  

Nr. 2 makes actually working on the site within RStudio quite annoying, since I already use `hugo serve` in the terminal I end up having two localhosts of the same site running (and I'd prefer keep using the terminal explicitly). Is there a way to choose this to not happen through some unknown option? I would rather not have my manual knitting starting a daemon (which in my opinion is quite unexpected behaviour when manually kntting. I also cannot see the standard R Markdown knitting information in the R markdown pane that I would usually see).

title: Knitting with the Button in the IDE renders HTML even with method != 'html'
description:
It seems there is something we don't expect in RStudio IDE when using the knit button with blogdown.

blogdown offer different rendering method like 
* method = "custom"
* method = "markdown"

However, even with this method, a HTML is produced when it should not be **only when using the knit button**

This steps should help reproduce 

* Open a new example site to no break anything.
* Use `options(blogdown.method = "custom")` in .Rprofile. This should tell blogdown to let the `build.R` script do the rendering. 
* Restart and check `blogdown:::build_method()` is `"custom"`
* leave `build.R` empty - as do nothing. 
* `blogdown::build_site(build_rmd = TRUE)` will correctly do nothing
* Use the Knit button on a Rmd post => The HTML file will be rendered 

It is the same with `method = "markdown"`

I was under the impression that the Knit button in the IDE would run `rmarkdown::render_site(<absolut_input_path>)` but 

* running `rmarkdown::render_site(<absolut_input_path>)` in the R console will correctly output a .md file
* Clicking on the knit button will run the same function, but in the Rmarkdown pane and will output .html

This happens only with .Rmd to .md - .Rmarkdown are correctly rendered to .markdown. 

It is as if the IDE is modifying the behavior somehow. IDE bug ? 

Discovered in https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/530

description:

I've been working a lot with blogdown over the past week, and realized one thing that led me to some errors introduced by over-page-refreshing. title: Getting started with Wowchemy
description:
In the `NEWS.md` it says:

> When creating a new site with blogdown::new_site(), the theme gcushen/hugo-academic is automatically redirected to wowchemy/starter-academic, because the original Github repo has moved and become a repo of Hugo modules.

So `new_site("gcushen/hugo-academic")` does work, which takes care of folks stumbling upon old docs, tutorials, etc. But the following do not work, which are currently the easiest to discover via Wowchemy docs <https://wowchemy.com/docs/install/>:

`new_site(theme = "wowchemy/starter-academic")`

`new_site(theme = "wowchemy/starter-blog")`

`new_site(theme = "wowchemy/starter-book")`

`new_site(theme = "wowchemy/wowchemy-hugo-modules")`

(I realize why these don't work in theory as none are repos that contain actual Hugo themes (!!!), but not sure if any user could ever figure this out now in practice if they haven't used Hugo themes before, especially as no repository named `gcushen/hugo-academic` exists currently.)

description:

This feature request originally comes from a discussion in RStudio Community: https://community.rstudio.com/t/how-to-share-output-yml-among-blodwon-posts-when-blogdown-new-bundle-is-true/91557

title: Recommended way to serve the site?
description:
I typically use the Add-in to serve the site, and I just noticed that `serve_site()` appears to be an [exported function](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/2b1449d0217aa4348aaa6bf9e0b0d5763921a509/R/serve.R#L16-L55).

Yet, when I use the Add-in, this prints to my console:

```
blogdown:::serve_site()
```

But then sometimes when I'm editing a blog post, this prints to my console:

```
blogdown:::preview_site()
```


Reading the actual function definition [here](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/2b1449d0217aa4348aaa6bf9e0b0d5763921a509/R/serve.R#L65-L85), I see why they are different. But I was confused. I think we want to encourage `serve_site()` to start? If so, I cannot see where to change where those `:::` print to the console.

title: Support downlit for syntax highlighting
description:
With the recent developments in blogdown, one area where a difference remains between {hugodown} and {distill} on one side and {blogdown} on the other is syntax highlighting. 

The approach taken by {distill} and {hugodown} via {downlit} seems to me quite effective - in terms of ease of setup as well as output (esp. linking and better sensitivity to R-specific syntax). A useful way of implementing presumably would be to allow opting in or out (depending on what a safe default is) to accommodate those using other syntax highlighting tools.

I haven't seen this discussed anywhere with respect to {blogdown}, so: would a {downlit} integration in {blogdown} be feasible and is it perhaps being considered? title: Allow user to specify "dir" in calls to serve_site
description:
This is somewhat related to item number 15. described in the [wishlist for 0.21](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/476#issue-706980859). 

I've recently started creating my own blog. Actually my own 2 blogs. One for my R stuff (package devel. problems, riddles, interesting things I've had to answer from Stackoverflow and so forth), and one for my side-project which is learning French (oh my god.. could a language have any more grammer?! O.o). At the moment both are still babies, but I am starting to work on them side-by-side to combine my love for R with my poor skills at French grammer.

I started my process by creating a blog for my R stuff, duplicated the repository and changed a few things around. While everything was fine while I worked on a single project, while I'm working on 2 I tend to get frustrated by the fact that I can't specify the directory (`dir`) in `server::server_config` through `serve_site`. 

Currently the code works by searching for the `config.toml` starting in `getwd()`. While minor it seems natural for "serve_site" to allow one to specify the directory or starting point for `blogdown:::site_root` (the function that is currently used for finding the directory)

# So I want:
An argument (example: `.site_dir`) for the function `serve_site` to specify the directory where I have my blog
# What is needed for this to work?
The argument would need to be added to `serve_site`, the function output by `serve_it` and `site_root`
# What would it do?
The argument would allow one to start the site from any directory, for example if one had a site in `/A/B/C/D/E/F/` one could start the site while the working directory (`getwd()`) was `/G/H/I/` by executing `serve_site(.site_dir = '/A/B/C/D/E/F/')`.
# What consequences would this have for the existing code base?
The code base would need approximately 5 extra lines of code, and as long as the default argument goes to `getwd()`  and the argument is added after the formal `...` this addition would not affect current users of `blogdown` who are happy with the current behaviour.

# Have you added a pull request?
I have already forked, implemented and tested the code necessary for this feature. A pull request will be linked (here) once I've uploaded the change.

title: Adding checking functions to help users check their sites themselves
description:
🤕 Problem: there are lots of (predictable) ways that blogdown users can stumble into pain. We have added some printed messages like errors and warnings to help teach users, but the problem with those is that users still experience pain first. They may get frustrated and give up early, or start to tune out these “helpful” messages.

Proposed solution: take a more proactive stance to guide users toward success first by offering some targeted functions to help them sidestep predictable pain points, while at the same time helping users understand all the moving pieces. We could perhaps offer individual checking functions, then wrap them all up in a larger `check_site()` function? The key here would be printing the output in a user-friendly way.



1. `check_config()`

   - Do they have `unsafe = TRUE`? 

   - Do they have a `baseURL` set? 

   - Do they have `ignoreFiles = _files$`?

1. `check_gitignore()`

   - Did they ignore the right files? 

   - OK to ignore: `blogdown`, `public`, `resources` (if `netlify.toml` exists)

   - NOT OK to ignore: `*.html` files,  `*.md` files, the `static/` directory 

1. `check_hugo()` (see `options(blogdown.hugo.version = xxx)`)

   - What version Hugo are you running with blogdown?

   - What is the minimum version of Hugo that your theme requires?

   - Have multiple local Hugo versions? If so, advise how to clean them up.

1. `check_netlify()` (see `options(blogdown.check.netlify = FALSE)`)

   - What `HUGO_VERSION` do you have in your `netlify.toml`?

   - Is it the same as your local Hugo version that blogdown is using?

   - Does the publish directory match `config.toml`?

1. `check_content()` (see `options(blogdown.check.html = FALSE)`)

   - **Draft/future content:** Check for content marked as draft or with a future publish date; list and advise (see `options(blogdown.warn.future = FALSE)` and `options(blogdown.draft.output = TRUE)`)

   - **Forgot to knit:** Check for source files with no rendered file versions 

   - **Bad knitted `.html`:** Detect `.html` files that seem to be generated by clicking the Knit button in RStudio with blogdown < v0.21; list and advise

   - **Duplicate `.md` + `.html` files:** users often “double render” and Hugo by default shows the `.html` over the `.md`. Confusing to debug.

   - **Source/output out-of-sync:** source is newer than output (see `options(blogdown.files_filter = blogdown:::md5sum_filter/blogdown:::timestamp_filter)`)

Thoughts? Any pitfalls I've missed? Other ideas for achieving similar outcomes?

title: Improve behavior of RStudio IDE Build Website button
description:
# Context

This is first from a question in the community: 
https://community.rstudio.com/t/css-formatting-not-showing-when-building-blogdown-new-site/89672/3
then from a discussion with @apreshill 

## Clinking Build Website 

Currently, clicking the Build Website button will 
 * run, `rmarkdown::render_site(encoding = 'UTF-8')`
 * This will run `blogdown:::blogdown_site()[["render"]]`,
 *  that will run `blogdown::build_site()`
It means it will build a blogdown website ready for publishing in the `public/`folder, but it won't be easily previewable. It is a choice. 
But current issue is an undesired behavior IMO: RStudio IDE will the website in the viewer. I don't know exactly where this is done, but I am guessing the IDE will open in the viewer the output of `rmarkdown::render_site()`. 

With **blogdown**, this is problematic as it won't be correctly previewed - it would require running a local server (`servr` as before, or `hugo server`)

It seems there is not current way to deactivate 

### What could be done ? 

Several options I think: 

1. Deactivate the previewing - to see with the IDE team ? 
2. Configure the preview to be run with a custom function in the package - not possible today. This would allow to run a local server for this
3. Combining 1 and 2: On a condition (`preview = TRUE` for example in the site_generator), `rmarkdown::render_site()` would run the `render` function of the site generator and considering the preview will be dealt with so skipping the "open in preview" step. 

Regarding what we could expect from the Build Website button for **blogdown**, I would suggest with @apreshill feedback: 
* To build the website as we would do for publishing (like drag & drop on netlify) AND having the hability to preview before publishing. 
That would mean no draft post, no future post. Something like 
```sh
hugo server --bind <host> -p <port> --themesDir <themeDir> -t <theme> -d <publishdir> --cleanDestinationDir
```

But obviously that would mean being able to customize the behavior of the button more precisely 🤷 

I opened this to discuss it and gather ideas

Related to #518 which is the Clean All button in the IDE

title: Update <pre class="name"> to <code class=lang->
description:
I was trying to use prism.js for syntax highligthing with blogdown. However, on prism.js website they say:

> Prism does its best to encourage good authoring practices. Therefore, it only works with `<code>` elements, since marking up code without a `<code>` element is semantically invalid. According to the HTML5 spec, the recommended way to define a code language is a language-xxxx class, which is what Prism uses. Alternatively, Prism also supports a shorter version: lang-xxxx.

Looking at the html that blogdown generates, the name of the language goes in `<pre class=> `. This looks like to be due to the way pandoc does (see [this issue](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/3858)), so one easy fix would be to wait to pandoc be updated.

Is there a way to do it? The topic I linked above suggests using a lua filter, but I could not make it work. I tried using the `pandoc_args` in the yaml header, for example:

```
output:
  blogdown::html_page:
    pandoc_args:
      [
      "--lua-filter=script.lua"]
```
 I also read on the manual that one could configure build tools and it might be the way to do it, but I never did it before. 

One might be tempted to change prism.js itself, however maybe making the files that blogdown generates comply with HTML5 specification might be interesting in itself.

Thanks in advance and thanks for the awesome package

I have a folder named "source" that contains all the pre-build files, and I build to a different folder located at ../githubname/ from there. **Clean All** deleted the githubname folder completely, including a lot of other important files like various course notes that were not part of the bookdown output and were not added to my github repository, so I (apparently) have no way of recovering them now. The working directory, in the console at least, was the source folder, so I don't know why it would have deleted the contents of a different folder.

I may have lost a lot of valuable work permanently and I hope to alert the project maintainers to prevent this happening to others.

I can't give a reprex because I can't recover the state before the issue occurred.

title: install_hugo does not check the version when checking for already installed version
description:
When you try to run a blogdown site with the wrong hugo version, you now get an error message 
```r
<error/rlang_error>
Erreur : Found 'hugo' at 'C:\Users\chris\scoop\shims\hugo.exe' but its version is 0.78.2 instead of the requested version 0.76.5. You may try blogdown::install_hugo("0.76.5").
Backtrace:
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see the full context.
```

The advice is to run `blogdown::install_hugo()` with correct version, but without `force = TRUE` it won't install the asked version. 
```r
168 MiB [<no git>] > blogdown::install_hugo("0.76.5")
It seems Hugo has been installed. Use force = TRUE to reinstall or upgrade.*
```
So it is one more step to run 
```r
blogdown::install_hugo("0.76.5", force = TRUE)
```

before being able to preview the website which had a pinned hugo version. 

I think we should either: 
* add `force = TRUE` in the error message advice
* make `install_hugo` only message with `'It seems Hugo has been installed. Use force = TRUE to reinstall or upgrade.'` if the version is the same as the one provided in `version = `

What do you think ?

title: Improve error/warning messages
description:
After running into many error/warning messages with `v0.21.42`, I think we can improve these to make the user experience better and make the message more readable and actionable cc @cderv 

For example, I got this error:

> The 'publish' setting in 'netlify.toml' is 'public/' but the publish dir in the Hugo config file is 'public'. You may want to change the former to the latter.

The printing and phrasing of this messages (in addition to the volume of messages that get printed to my console when I serve the site) makes it hard to understand what is being checked, compared, and what I should do to make the warning go away. It would be nice if the printed message were more user-friendly and formatted nicely in the console, like usethis messages that use [cli](https://cli.r-lib.org/) and [crayon](https://github.com/r-lib/crayon). Something like this:

```
✓ Checking `netlify.toml` file, set 'publish = docs' 
✓ Checking `config.toml` file, set 'publishDir = publish' 
✓ Comparing `netlify.toml` and `config.toml` publish directories
● Warning: publish directories do not match. We recommend editing 
your `config.toml` file to set 'publishDir = docs'.  
```


Similarly:
```
✓ Checking `blogdown::hugo_version()`, set as `0.71.1`
✓ Checking `netlify.toml` file, set `HUGO_VERSION = 0.65.0`
✓ Comparing `blogdown` and `netlify.toml` Hugo versions
● Warning: Hugo versions do not match. We recommend editing 
your `netlify.toml` file to set `HUGO_VERSION = 0.71.1`. 
If you do not wish to edit the `netlify.toml` file, you may instead use 
`blogdown::install_hugo("0.65.0")` to change your local Hugo version.
```

And for Hugo installations, I see:
> Warning message: Found hugo at "/Users/alison/Library/Application Support/Hugo/0.71.1/hugo" and "/usr/local/bin/hugo". The former will be used. If you don't need both copies, you may delete/uninstall the latter. 

It would be great if it looked more like:
```
✓ Checking local Hugo installations
✓ Copy #1 found at "/Users/alison/Library/Application Support/Hugo/0.71.1/hugo"
✓ Copy #2 found at "/usr/local/bin/hugo"
● Warning: multiple Hugo installations found; using copy #1. 
If you don't need both copies, you may uninstall copy #2 with _______.

Also, this message always prints twice for me:

```
> blogdown:::serve_site()
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
You are recommended to ignore more items in the 'ignoreFiles' field in config.toml: "\\.Rmd$", "\\.Rmarkdown$", "\\.knit\\.md$", "\\.utf8\\.md$"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

You are recommended to remove the item '_files$' in the 'ignoreFiles' field in config.toml.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

This is also quite long, I wonder if we could wrap in an argument to `serve_site` like `verbose` that defaults to `FALSE`?:

Launching the server via the command:

title: Detecting the publish directory via netlify.toml and config.toml
description:
Re: this feature:

> When a website is built or served for the first time in an R session, blogdown will check Netlify configurations if the file netlify.toml exists. Specifically, it will check if the local Hugo version matches the version specified in netlify.toml (in the environment variable HUGO_VERSION), and if the publish setting in netlify.toml matches the publishDir setting in Hugo's config file (if it is set). Hints will be printed if potential problems are found. If you think these messages are not helpful and can be ignored, you may suppress the check via the global option options(blogdown.check.netlify = FALSE).

I just saw this error using `v0.21.42`:

> The 'publish' setting in 'netlify.toml' is 'public/' but the publish dir in the Hugo config file is 'public'. You may want to change the former to the latter.

First, I don't have the publish dir set in my `config.toml` file, so the message is confusing (also the phrasing of the above message doesn't tell you which file is the "Hugo configuration file"- it should probably instead read "your `config.toml` file"). Also, I happen to know that the toml key there is `publishdir`, but many people will not know to look in the `config.toml` file for this key. So the "hint" feels more like an easter egg hunt, and I think we can make this easier.

Second, since the Netlify docs (<https://docs.netlify.com/configure-builds/file-based-configuration/#sample-file>) show the example with the trailing slash, this function should probably allow the trailing slash in the `netlify.toml`.

Third, the message printing and phrasing makes it hard to understand what is being checked, compared, and what I should do to make the warning go away. It would be nice if the printed message were more user-friendly and formatted nicely in the console, like usethis messages that use [cli](https://cli.r-lib.org/). I'll file another issue for this cc @cderv.

title: Blogdown with a mix of html_document & flex_dashboard
description:
I built a blogdown site using Hugo and it has multiple sections, posts all written in Rmarkdown with outputs designed as html_document. It works fine.

In parallel, I designed an HTML dashboard using Rmarkdown with an output designed as flex_dashboard. It generates an HTML file working fine.

I wanted to integrate the dashboard directly within the building of the site but unfortunately by simply adding the Rmarkdown file in the blogdown structure it knits it as an html document and not as a flex_dashboard. So, I have the content within my website but not at all as dashboard but more like a traditional html_document. So no luck with that :(

I tried then copying the dashboard html under /static/html and create a brand new Rmarkdown just invoking my html within an iframe:
```

--- 
output: html_document
---
<link rel="preload" href="/html/OpenDashboard.html" as="document">
<iframe width="100%" height="600" name="iframe" src="/html/OpenDashboard.html"></iframe>
```

Looked good to me and was pretty happy even in inelegant but performance is bad. It takes a long time to load (+10sec) even if the file is not that big (only 6Mb). Size of the html will grow a lot in the future and I can't hope viewers will wait that long.

I read it was possible to clarify the type of knitting we want within a build.R file but I am clueless on how to specify I want html_document knitting for some Rmarkdowns and flex_dashboard for some others.

For info, the website is www.opensourcepv.com and the dashboard in integrated using an iframe under https://www.opensourcepv.com/opendashboard/

title: Netlify & Post-production R script
description:
Hi all,
I hope this will make some sense! :-)
So: I have a site in `blogdown`, which I then deploy in `Netlify` [https://stats-he.netlify.app/](https://stats-he.netlify.app/). All works like a charm. However, I have written an `R` script to post-process the build to modify some text in the `public/` folder. My apologies if this is trivial and/or I've missed something obvious!
Thanks
Gianluca

title: Website in Viewer is updated before Rmd rendering
description:
I believe with `blogdown.knit.on_save` activated, the viewer is reloaded **before** the Rmd is rerendered with the change. At least, in most of the time and on Windows.

This cause the viewer to not show the last change but the previous one. 

## Steps when this happens

See #481 for full workflow

* Open a new blodown project with auto build activated
* Hugo server starts on the homepage
* Navigate in the viewer to the post you want to modify
* Modify the Rmd file and Save 
* The viewer blink and does not show last change. However, the post is correctly rerendered 
```r
Rendering content/post/2015-07-23-r-rmarkdown.Rmd... Done.
```
* Add another modification in the Rmd file and save
* The viewer is updated but show the first change that was made  and not the one we just did.
* Manually reload the viewer - you are sent back to the homepage
* Navigate to the post - change is there 

Maybe related to --navigateToChanged not working ? 

Let's note that it works ok if the post is opened in the browser 

There is something not stable in this I believe. I'll look into it based on these notes.

title: when using processx and we restart R, all the child processes are not killed
description:
This follows https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/480#issuecomment-705467866_

Here are the steps

* On windows, use processx and an installation with Shims (Scoop or chocolatey)
* Open a blogdown project, Hugo server will be launched
```r
> blogdown:::preview_site(startup = TRUE)
Launching the server via the command:
  hugo server --bind 127.0.0.1 -p 4321 --themesDir themes -t hugo-lithium -D -F --navigateToChanged
Serving the directory . at http://127.0.0.1:4321
Launched the hugo server in the background (process ID: 28916). To stop it, call blogdown::stop_server() or restart the R session.
```
* Check the open processes 
```r
> p <- ps::ps_handle(as.integer(blogdown:::opts$get("pids")))
> p
<ps::ps_handle> PID=28916, NAME=hugo.exe, AT=2020-10-08 10:06:56
> ps::ps_children(p)
[[1]]
<ps::ps_handle> PID=40476, NAME=hugo.exe, AT=2020-10-08 10:06:56

[[2]]
<ps::ps_handle> PID=41440, NAME=conhost.exe, AT=2020-10-08 10:06:56
```
* Try to restart - RStudio is freezing and does not manage to restart. Check processes in Powershell. The principal process 28916 (the scoop shim) is closed but the childs are not
```powershell
❯ Get-process -Id 28916,40476,41440 | Format-table -Property Id,ProcessName,HasExited

   Id ProcessName HasExited
   -- ----------- ---------
28916                  True
41440 conhost         False
40476 hugo            False
```

* Kill one of the child and Rstudio will unfreeze
```powershell
kill 40476
```

I guess that follows my comment on https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/commit/64d5f46ad0e38a9b399661ca1bcd465763a450bf#commitcomment-43062896

I think processx is killing the main process without the child, and reg.finalizer in bookdown does nothing. 

I'll check that and suggest a fix

title: Testing server feature and auto mode on/off - using the knit button
description:
@yihui I wanted to share the workflow of what I tested so far to see if this is the correct behavior for you.

## How it works for me

* Open a blogdown project (default one from Create Project)
* This will open a server: 
    * `blogdown:::preview_site(startup = TRUE)` is ran in the console
    * The website opens in the viewer on homepage
* Modify a Rmd post and save
* _With a delay the very first time_, this is printed and the post is rendered 
```
# printed in the console
Rendering content/post/2015-07-23-r-rmarkdown.Rmd... Done.

title: v0.21 wishlist
description:
Hi @yihui,

As we discussed, I'm plopping my wishlist for blogdown here. It is quite long! I use blogdown every day with multiple teams within and outside of RStudio, and I teach it a lot too. While I believe addressing these items would improve the user experience, I also understand that there is a lot here and I'm realistic that not all of them will be feasible to tackle 😄 

- [x] 1. Two of my biggest previous pain points have been resolved recently :tada:: hitting the preview button in RStudio for `.md` files generating an errant `.html` file, and not being able to use the knit button.

- [x] 2. We also got the IDE issue fixed where the page you navigated to in the viewer pane did not carry over when you opened the site in a full browser window; see https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/6967. 

- [x] 3. Develop a system for versioning Hugo for each website project. I often have a few Hugo websites that I jump into on any given day, and sometimes I need to update Hugo to make one theme work, but I explicitly cannot update Hugo for another site b/c the theme isn't compatible with the latest Hugo. This situation is hard 😿 I would love for blogdown to help users manage this realistic situation better. [[related issue](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/50)]

- [x] 4. Along the same lines, develop a way to help users keep the local Hugo version in sync with the Netlify version (if using). [hugodown](https://github.com/r-lib/hugodown/blob/master/R/hugo-version.R) introduced a check on the `netlify.toml` file if present to make sure that you had the same version of Hugo running locally as you have set in the `netlify.toml` file for the build. This is huge for teams b/c you often have many people posting (and using blogdown/Hugo) quite sporadically, so this saves the site maintainer from having to be a lifeguard and jump in whenever there is a Hugo version mismatch.

- [x] 5. Fix the blogdown system for detecting changes to the source files (i.e., the pain of serving site and blogdown reknitting en masse). I have had several sites in various stages of paralysis because blogdown tries to reknit posts that already had rendered versions and the source post had not been edited. This is a pretty common story, and appears to be more prevalent for folks who use Github, especially with multiple collaborators. I believe this was a primary source of pain for the tidyverse team, and why [hugodown](https://hugodown.r-lib.org/index.html#usage) has the two-step rendering by design, where you knit with intention. [[see also](https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyverse.org/tree/ee03715f1038d0c594bf0d4f3ac000f22b5fecc4#troubleshooting)]

- [x] 6. Develop better system for dealing with post dependencies. They currently all ship off to `static/`, which can be hard to debug when you cannot tell which post used which version of which lib. hugodown treated each post as its own project, and so the libs folders populated within each post bundle, which I found a pleasant way to work. For example, this is what the `rmarkdown-libs/` folder looks like for the [tidymodels.org](https://github.com/tidymodels/tidymodels.org/tree/master/static/rmarkdown-libs) site, and it was hard for me to connect these with the right content. [[related issue]](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/469)

- [x] 7. Better support of post bundles. Post bundles were a great Hugo innovation that happened after the original package design/release. I realize that may mean changing a [default option](https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/more-global-options.html), but most people simply don't know what a post bundle is. Also, when you add the sample `.Rmd` post, it usually looks very odd in the directory structure of the example site, because most current Hugo themes have example sites with bundled posts. So it would also be good to have the example post be a post bundle itself, perhaps with a single static file and some text in the post itself about what it is and how to use it. I'm happy to contribute this if you agree with the idea.

- [ ] 8. Simplify the input file formats. This figure by Emi Tanaka sums it up well, but it also reveals why it is confusing: https://emitanaka.org/r/posts/2018-12-12-scientific-and-technical-blogging-radix-vs-blogdown/#fig:blogdown. I would definitely support treating markdown output as the default, or at least making `.md` easier to output. For all the reasons we say markdown is better than HTML at readability, diff-ability, etc. It feels more future-proof. This was one of the design decisions for [hugodown](https://hugodown.r-lib.org/index.html#compared-to-blogdown), and it feels like there may be a happy middle where blogdown can be more md-focused. [[related issue](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/445)]

- [ ] 9. Figure out a way for the Hugo `.TableOfContents` variable to populate from `.Rmd` (if knitting to `.html`). Currently, this is another of my reasons for strictly using `.Rmarkdown` content instead of `.Rmd`. This variable is commonly used across many themes (including my own), so it feels important to figure out (I think you mentioned at one point it may require some JavaScript?) [[related issue](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/267)] [[related issue](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/165)] [[related issue](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/58)]

- [x] 10. Better support Netlify integration. I really liked the [hugodown::use_netlify_toml()](https://hugodown.r-lib.org/reference/use_netlify_toml.html) function, which populated a file from [here](https://github.com/r-lib/hugodown/blob/master/inst/templates/netlify.toml). I configure my own a bit differently, but this is a very nice and simple function to offer. It would be great to pre-populate this file with the Hugo version pulling from what is there locally, to start with.

- [x] 11. Along the same lines, a simple function to add the [`build.R`](https://blogdown-demo.rbind.io/2017/09/06/adding-r-markdown-documents-of-other-output-formats/) file in project root, or have it come as default with all blogdown sites. This for me is still one of my top blogdown features --- so small yet so impactful.

- [ ] 12. Show the output format in new posts by default, but make an option to remove it from future posts when using the add-in or function for new posts. This helps folks troubleshoot, as it is currently difficult to figure out and to search for.

- [x] 13. Update or retire the add image add-in. It was really helpful when all images had to be in `static/`, but now it is just confusing. If keep, make it be smart about page bundles, and perhaps follow the same UI as the visual markdown editor.

- [ ] 14. Small, but given that we warn about draft posts, perhaps if serve site is running, print a warning when a user creates a new content folder named something not currently in layouts (like: _"warning- found no layout file for content section named `xxx`; your theme’s default layout will be used unless you change the file's [type](https://gohugo.io/content-management/types/) or write a new Hugo layout- do you still wish to continue? Learn about Hugo layout lookup orders here: https://gohugo.io/templates/lookup-order"_). Or something along those lines. I feel that the Hugo layout lookup orders are pretty hard to grasp onto for anyone who isn't a Hugo theme developer. [[related issue from Hugo repo](https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/6636)]

- [ ] 15. Support and recognize [configuration directories](https://gohugo.io/getting-started/configuration/#configuration-directory). Currently, blogdown moves the `config.toml` to the root- is it possible to support it inside a config directory? The setup makes it difficult for users to use Netlify's "Deploy to Netlify" button that theme developers sometimes offer (which is so nice!), and often means that theme set-up instructions and other example repos don't match up for unwitting users.

- [ ] 16. I would love for HTML widgets to work more reliably. I have heard that [shadowdom](https://github.com/jcheng5/shadowdom) could be a possible helper here, but this is an ongoing source of pain for myself and many users.

- [ ] 17. Enable an easier way to edit layout files. The better practice is to copy the layout file from the `themes/` directory then place it in project root and edit *that* version. But this is annoying with clicking in the IDE, especially when you are teaching or doing it everyday. Would it be possible to provide a simple function like `edit_layout("post", template = c("list", "single", "all"))` that copies the folders from the theme's directory and plops them into the project root for editing? 

- [x] 18. Add a pkgdown site (assigned to self 😉)

- [ ] 19. Update the book (also assigned to self 😉  )

Thanks for considering these, and I'm happy to explain my context and thinking on any of these if helpful. And of course, looking forward to contributing.

Alison

P.S. including some blog posts by experienced users that I think offer good insights:

+ <https://clauswilke.com/blog/2020/09/08/a-blogdown-post-for-the-ages/>
+ <https://drmowinckels.io/blog/2020-05-25-changing-you-blogdown-workflow/>
+ <https://masalmon.eu/2020/02/29/hugo-maintenance/>
+ <https://yutani.rbind.io/post/2017-10-25-blogdown-custom/>

title: Use each blog post's renv environment when rendering
description:
Right now (and please correct me if I'm wrong) blogdown uses the global R environment when it's rendering each blog post.

Would it be possible to make blogdown use each blog post's local R environment (specifically `renv`) instead?

I am suggesting something along these lines:
+ blogdown's render "chain" `build_rms() -> render_page() -> render_page.R -> rmarkdown::render()` should `cd` into each blog post directory, and read any `./.Rprofile` so as to load `renv` if it is used for that blog post.

This way, I think blogdown would achieve several benefits. In particular, re-running blogdown would be less prone to break stuff (making blogdown behave a little more like [distill](https://rstudio.github.io/distill/) in that regard, effectively inoculating each blog post against changing package versions). But it would also make it much easier to have only certain blog posts use specific package versions without having to muddle the global R installation.

What follows are the steps I took to test if blogdown uses `renv`'s environment if a blog post specifies one (please correct me if I'm missing something).

As a simple test, I have created a new blog post for my existing blog using RStudio 1.3 (by creating a new project, and checking "use renv"). Then I created a plot that uses ggrepel's `segment.curvature` functionality (which is available in the latest dev version, but gives a warning message "unknown parameter" in the CRAN version).

So inside the project/blog post (which uses renv):
```
> renv::install("slowkow/ggrepel")
> packageVersion("ggrepel")
[1] ‘0.9.0’
```
and compiling the blog post using RStudio yields the expected curved ggrepel segments and no warning messages.

But when re-compiling the site with blogdown, the warning message is seen in the CLI output, and the resulting plot uses straight segments instead of nicely curved ones. And I can easily confirm that my global R environment uses the CRAN version of ggrepel:
```
> packageVersion("ggrepel")
[1] ‘0.8.2’
```

To re-iterate my point: would it be possible to make blogdown support `renv` for each blog post?
