title: Call build_site() but only render 'new' pages like what happens with serve_site()
description:
---

<!--
Please keep the below portion in your issue. Your issue will be closed if any of the above boxes is not checked. In certain (rare) cases, you may be exempted if you give a brief explanation (e.g., you are only making a suggestion for improvement). Thanks!
-->

Hi - I'm asking a question rather than an issue here. I'm trying to call `build_site()` but only render pages where the `.Rmd` file is newer than the `.html` file, similar to what happens in `serve_site()`. 

This relates to using github actions to periodically update a specific page on my site and rebuild it before publishing to Netlify. The specific reason for this is that I have one page that I want to update every day as it pulls in new data and updates a table and chart. 

This is entirely possible to do locally by simply having a script that does something like the following and manually running it each day.

```
library(blogdown)
blogdown:::touch_file('path_to_page.Rmd')
blogdown::serve_site()
```

If I run this locally and commit the changes, then Netlify will rebuild the site and everything will be updated. What I'm trying to do is replicate the above workflow using github actions so that I don't have to do it manually. 

I can get pretty close but I think running `blogdown::serve_site()` doesn't work within the github actions workflow. I asked this question (in a bit more of a convoluted way) on [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62825976/using-blogdown-with-github-actions-alternative-to-serve-site) but haven't received a response. 

For my github actions setup, I can use the following

```
name: Get new data and rebuild site

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 13 * * 1"
  push:
    branches:
      - master

jobs:
  scrape-and-commit:
    runs-on: macOS-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@master
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v1
      - name: Install packages
        run: Rscript -e 'install.packages("blogdown")'
      - name: Install Hugo
        run: Rscript -e 'blogdown::install_hugo(extended = TRUE, version = "0.66.0")'
      - name: Touch files
        run: Rscript -e 'blogdown:::touch_file("path_to_file.Rmd)' 
      - name: Build site
        run: Rscript -e 'blogdown::serve_site()'
```

(note - I haven't shown the github commit part of the workflow). 

This seems to just cancel itself after a while, I suspect because `serve_site()` is meant to be run locally to render a preview which probably doesn't work on the virtual machine. 

```
Serving the directory /Users/runner/work/plussixoneblog/plussixoneblog at http://127.0.0.1:4321
##[error]The operation was canceled.
```

I could in theory run `blogdown::build_site()` here instead but my big problem is that I don't want every post or page re-rendered. I just want to render the file that I _touched_. The reason being that the older posts/pages reference data that has since changed and I don't want them updated. 

So basically - I'm wondering if there is a way to replicate the `serve_site` ability to just render files where the `.Rmd` file is newer than the `.html` file without rendering the site locally? Or - has anyone else had any luck using github actions/netlify to rebuild just parts of a site rather than the whole thing?

title: Pandoc rules regarding LaTeX not followed consistently
description:
I can create a new blogdown site utilizing the default [hugo-lithium][1] theme and the text statement below will not render as a LaTeX equation, which is the behavior I expect. 

`An amount between $5 and $10.`

[Pandoc's manual](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#math) explains the reason why, which I'll paste below with a bold emphasis:

> Anything between two `$` characters will be treated as TeX math. The opening `$` must have a non-space character immediately to its right, **while the closing `$` must have a non-space character immediately to its left, and must not be followed immediately by a digit**. Thus, `$20,000 and $30,000` won’t parse as math. If for some reason you need to enclose text in literal `$` characters, backslash-escape them and they won’t be treated as math delimiters.

HOWEVER, I can change to other Hugo themes (e.g. [hugo-theme-codex][2]) and this exact same text block renders improperly whenever I include `math: true` in my YAML.

`An amount between $5 and $10.` ends up displaying as:

[![latex and rmd][3]][3]

Why is LaTeX invoked, when Pandoc is supposed to follow the rule I quoted above? How can I use "other" hugo themes, still use LaTeX math equations, and have Pandoc follow it's own rules? Escaping the `$` unfortunately doesn't do anything, and displays the same result as the un-escaped version.

```
# Doesn't work
An amount between \$5 and \$10.
```

[![latex and rmd][3]][3]

Getting in on the double slash escape action doesn't seem to work either:

```
# Doesn't work
An amount between \\$5 and \\$10.
```

[![double slash image][4]][4]

  [1]: https://github.com/yihui/hugo-lithium
  [2]: https://github.com/jakewies/hugo-theme-codex
  [3]: https://i.stack.imgur.com/jCMU6m.png
  [4]: https://i.stack.imgur.com/A8IG8m.png
  [5]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62917217/r-markdown-inline-latex-equations-vs
  [6]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62915849/cant-escape-latex-dollar-sign-in-blogdown

---

title: Math expressions do not require protection in backticks
description:
Currently `blogdown` wraps all math expressions in backticks using `blogdown:::process_file(out2, xfun::protect_math)` to ensure correct rendering. For instance,

$$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$

renders as

```
`$$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$`
```

However in Hugo version 0.60+, it seems that this is no longer necessary. In fact the equation does not render when I do this. When I remove `blogdown:::process_file(out2, xfun::protect_math)` in `render_page.R`, the equation renders accurately

```
$$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$
```

Is it still necessary to include this protection in `blogdown`, or am I missing something? If it is not required, I can submit a pull request removing this element.

title: blogdown posts with renv renders Rmd files too greedily
description:
This is more of a feature request (or possibly a bug, depending on the project's goals).

At present, `build_site()` [finds and renders *all* Rmd files within the blog post's directory recursively (except for files beginning with underscore)](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/86ea620d6dfbe0f745ad89dc131b0dc6662e572c/R/render.R#L52). 

This makes it effectively impossible to use `build_site` if any blog post uses `renv::` (or `packrat::` for that matter). [I've raised this question on SE, including more details](https://stackoverflow.com/q/61323455/1198249) (before I figured to check the `build_site` source myself, duh). 

The problem is that the renv directory contains the full sources of R packages, and they are littered with Rmd files. Using `build_site` causes `rmarkdown::render` to happily render these files too.

By having each blog post in its own renv, my goal is to to "future-proof" site rebuilds, very much in line with the sentiment expressed by @maxheld83 in #50.

Would blogdown care to support this use of renv with each post out-of-the-box, so to speak? Or is this use case not common/expected?

If left to my own devices, I'd probably simply exclude `renv/` from the list of paths returned by `list_rmd` (something along the lines of `files[!grepl("renv/", files)]`). Don't hurt me :-)

title: keep_md option not used by blogdown::html_page
description:
Hi

I have noticed that `blogdown::html_page()` does not make use of the `keep_md` option. For example this YAML frontmatter does not result in a `.md` file as well as the `.html` file.

```
output:
  blogdown::html_page:
    keep_md: true
```

I believe this is related to this **rmarkdown** issue https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1558.

Not sure if this is the desired behaviour or not but there are two workarounds I have come up with.

Option 1 is create a new output format that checks for `keep_md` and passes other options on to `blogdown::html_page()`.

```r
html_page_with_md <- function(..., number_sections = FALSE,
                                self_contained = FALSE, highlight = NULL,
                                template = NULL, pre_knit = NULL,
                                post_processor = NULL) {
    opts <- list(...)
    keep_md <- ifelse(!is.null(opts$keep_md), opts$keep_md, FALSE)

    rmarkdown::output_format(
        knitr       = NULL,
        pandoc      = NULL,
        keep_md     = keep_md,
        base_format = blogdown::html_page(
            ...,
            number_sections = number_sections,
            self_contained  = self_contained,
            highlight       = highlight,
            template        = template,
            pre_knit        = pre_knit,
            post_processor  = post_processor
        )
    )
}
```

The other option is to use `rmarkdown::resolve_output_format()` to get the output format and then manually set the `keep_md` option.

```r
output_format <- rmarkdown::resolve_output_format(input)
output_format$keep_md <- TRUE
```

I think this is probably the easiest option as long as you always want the `.md` file. The best solution would be for `blogdown::html_page()` to pass on the `keep_md` argument like above (if that is something you want to be able to do).

If there is a better solution please let me know.

title: Feature request: enableing link_attributes extension for .md files by default
description:
I understand that we can easily make links open in new browser tabs using `[link](URL){target="_blank"}` syntax as described on [Yihui's blog post](https://yihui.org/en/2018/09/target-blank/).

However, the [link_attributes extension](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#extension-link_attributes) is only enabled for `.Rmd` files; we can't employ this method against `.md` files unless we enable the extension in the call to pandoc with `+link_attributes`.

I was wondering if we could enable this link_attributes extension globally for both `.Rmd` and `.md` files within `blogdown` package.

I am requesting this because there are some required `.md` files shipped with hugo themes, which are not working when replaced with `.Rmd` files.

For example, [gcushen/hugo-academic](https://github.com/gcushen/hugo-academic) has its own skeleton `.md` file for users to create their admin profiles including their bios:

> "./content/authors/admin/_index.md"

Since my bio included some links that I wanted to open in new tabs, I appended `{target="_blank"}` to each of the link elements.

I found, however, that `blogdown::build_site()` did not work when I converted the `_index.md` file into a `.Rmd` format, which means I failed to secure a way to employ the `link_attributes` extension.

Please kindly consider this request.

title: Large posts/pages slow when using build_site, pandoc out of memory while running build_dir.
description:
I imagine other folks might be able to make use of this script so I am posting it here. I've seen Yihui post a similar script somewhere, but I am unable to find it.
It resolves pandoc out of memory errors I encountered in rendering large documents inside of the `static` folder that were being knitted when `build_dir` was called from within *build.R*.  It was also beginning to take upwards to 10m to build the site because there were so many dependency files inside of the project folder within *static* that were being copied to the public hugo directory needlessly. 

The script does the following:
 - It checks to see if the html file exists in the appropriate directory in the static folder and when the file was last modified.
 - If the file doesn't exist or is behind the Rmd doc from which it was rendered, it checks to see if there is a render of the Rmd doc inside the Rmd's local directory (one that might have been created for testing purposes to ensure the Rmd of the large document was rendering as intended) If the knitted html exists, and it's modified time is ahead of the Rmd, it simply copies this html file to the appropriate directory and renames it to *index.html*.
 - If there is no html file to copy, it will render the Rmd as a self-contained html file with the name *index.html* inside of the appropriate directory inside of the *static* folder
 - It will save a data.frame with a record of your files and their modified times in the root directory of the site with the name *Rmd_modification_times.csv*
 - It then build the *static* folder with `build_dir` which will just copy the self-contained html files in their respective directories to the hugo public folder.

Depends are `readr`, `purrr`, `fs` - if you have the `tidyverse` it should work fine. Note that `browser` is called so you will see a debug trace when running with `build_site` such that if errors are encountered you will have a good idea of where they occurred.

The solution is two part:
 1. Relocate the directory for large analyses (50+mb worth of files) to the root directory of the site, rather than the static folder.
 2. Use the following script, modifying accordingly:
```
f <- c(`[THE DIRECTORY INSIDE STATIC]` = "[THE PATH FROM BLOGDOWN ROOT TO/THE FILENAME.Rmd]",
       `[THE DIRECTORY INSIDE STATIC FOR FILE 2]` = "[THE PATH FROM BLOGDOWN ROOT TO/THE FILENAME.Rmd]")
f_mods <- purrr::imap_dfr(f, ~{
  #browser()
  # Get the rmd modified time
  .rmd_mod <- fs::file_info(.x)$modification_time
  # Construct the path to the live html file
  .live_html <- paste0(c("static", .y, "index.html"), collapse = "/")
  # Get the modified time of the live html file
  .live_html_mod <- fs::file_info(.live_html)$modification_time
  # Construct the path to the local html file
  .html <- paste0(dirname(.x), "/",stringr::str_sub(basename(.x), 1, -5), ".html")
  # Get the modified time of the local html file
  .html_mod <- fs::file_info(.html)$modification_time
  # If the live html file doesnt exist or is behind the rmd
  if (is.na(.live_html_mod) || .live_html_mod < .rmd_mod) {
    # If the local html file exists and is in front of the rmd
    if (!is.na(.html_mod) && .html_mod > .rmd_mod) {
      # Remove the old live html file
      if (!is.na(.live_html_mod)) file.remove(.live_html)
      # If the directory doesn't exist for the live file create it
      if (!dir.exists(dirname(.live_html))) fs::dir_create(dirname(.live_html))
      # Copy the local html file to the live file
      fs::file_copy(.html, .live_html)
    } else {
      # Otherwise render the rmd as index.html in the live directory
    rmarkdown::render(.x, output_file = "index.html", output_dir = paste0("static/", .y),intermediates_dir = dirname(.x), output_options = list(self_contained = T))
    }
  }
  # create the record
  data.frame(
    f = .y,
    rmd = .rmd_mod,
    html = .html_mod,
    live_html = .live_html_mod,
    stringsAsFactors = F
  )
})
# Save the record
readr::write_csv(f_mods, "Rmd_modification_times.csv")
blogdown::build_dir('static')
```

Ideally i would able to batch generate a set of pages from a template and have `blogdown::serve_site()` fill in the static pages. Even better would be to simply render everything on the fly, but I'm not sure how to make blogdown do that, or if it's even possible.

title: HTML tabbed sections
description:
I use blogdown to build my Hugo site and use rmarkdown to write posts.

rmarkdown allows content to be organized using tabs by applying .tabset class attribute to headers in a document. All sub-headers of the header with the .tabset attribute appear within tabs rather than as standalone sections.
See here:
https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/html-document.html#tabbed-sections

In long-form posts such as Exploratory Data Analysis, this feature allows sub-headers to be organized as tabs which makes them not only aesthetically pleasing but also a whole lot easier to read instead of endless scrolling.

At first, I though this was a hugo-academic theme issue so I posted this in that repo and got this response from the repo owner:
https://github.com/gcushen/hugo-academic/issues/1532#issuecomment-578250225

So it seems like blogdown doesn't convert .tabset headers when building the Hugo site, so the sub-headers within a header still require scrolling.

Is there a way to retain the sub-headers as tabs in a post? I tried looking at past open and closed issues in this repo to get any hints but it doesn't appear to have been discussed before.

I would appreciate any pointers.

Thank you!

@apreshill have noticed that, under some circumstances, the new post add-in is not using archetypes correctly. I think that it is related to page bundles. Here is a test site that shows the issue: https://github.com/malcolmbarrett/bundleexample. For this site, the add-in calls the archetype that is set up as a single `.md` file correctly but not for the one where it's bundled.

I'm not 100% sure, but after experimenting a bit, this seems to do with `hugo new`. It seems that if the path is a file name, it won't use the page bundle archetype, e.g. `hugo new dir -k myarchetype` works but `hugo new dir/mypost.md -k myarchetype` does not. 

A solution might be something like this, although I don't think the actual implementation can be quite this simple.

```
path = ifelse(utils::file_test("-d", kind), dirname(path), path)
# pass along to `hugo_cmd()` in some capacity...
```

Anyway, I'll wait on some guidance because I am uncertain about this issue, but I'm happy to try a PR if you agree with this diagnosis

title: blogdown:::serve_site() keeps opening new browser tabs
description:
When I write a new post for https://www.tidyverse.org, I generally use the "Serve Site" add-in, which calls `blogdown:::serve_site()`. It initially appears in RStudio's Viewer and I use "Show in New Window" to send it over to Safari. There, I navigate down to the post I'm working on. So far so good.

As I make edits and save, over in the `.Rmarkdown` file corresponding to the post, somehow the way I'm constantly rendering and previewing frequently (but not always?) results in a new tab being opened. It feels like it's because my existing Safari tab is not viewing the main page, but is viewing a specific post. That is just a theory. But it swiftly results in a crazy proliferation of browser tabs, conceivably one per "save".

description:

---

Hi @yihui,

Based on lots of trainings using the package lately, I'd like to request an improvement to often the earliest errors users receive. The issue is that many times individuals have already installed `blogdown` (and by extension, `hugo`), then perhaps didn't use it for awhile. Upon reusing the `new_site()` function (unsurprisingly), the hugo version is out of date and so nothing will work out of the box. The `hugo-academic` theme is the perfect example of this since the minimum version of hugo required is so recent. 

Many up-to-date themes include a `theme.toml` file (see: https://github.com/gohugoio/hugoThemes#themetoml), which specifies `min_version` of Hugo. I'm wondering if, when a user runs `new_site()` and selects a theme, `blogdown` could search for this file and do either:

1. Print with a clear error message what the minimum version is and how to upgrade ("Your theme requires a minimum Hugo version of XX. You are running version YY. Please use `update_hugo()` to upgrade your local Hugo version before continuing.")

1. if possible, since `new_site()` will install hugo if not installed, it would be awesome if it could update Hugo to `min_version` if a `theme_toml` file is detected.

title: Default position of external assets (JS/CSS) in HTML output is _blocking_
description:
## Issue

When I use htmlwidgets in my blogdown posts ([Plotly](https://github.com/ropensci/plotly/) to be more precise), the `<script>` and `<link>` tags to include their external JS/CSS dependencies are inserted right below the YAML metadata header. This is bad because it [blocks page rendering](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/30653081/why-scripts-at-the-end-of-body-tag/) until all these assets have been downloaded and processed by the browser. Adding the `async` or `defer` attribute to these `<script>` tags doesn't work because then the Plotly graphs aren't rendered anymore.

I'm using blogdown 0.11 with Hugo 0.55.6 and the [Universal Theme](https://github.com/devcows/hugo-universal-theme).

## Proposed solution

It would be better to include them _at the very end_ of the generated HTML file.
Even better would be some kind of integration into Hugo, so that the tags are actually placed _just before the end of `<body>`_ when Hugo generates the site. I don't really know how the latter could be achieved in a theme-agnostic way, though.

Anyway, I couldn't find an option or anything to control the position where these tags are inserted. Such an option would at least mitigate the problem. Additionally I'd suggest to change the default position to be the end of the generated document.

title: Images in Page Bundles Missing from RSS Feed
description: Version 0.1 changed the default behavior to use post bundles: > You can create a new post as the index file of a Hugo page bundle via blogdown::new_post() or the RStudio addin "New Post" if you set options(blogdown.new_bundle = TRUE). One benefit of using a page bundle instead of a normal page is that you can put resource files associated with the post (such as images) under the same directory of the post itself. This means you no longer have to put them under the static/ directory, which has been quite confusing to Hugo beginners (thanks, @DavisVaughan @romainfrancois @apreshill, #351). title: New post addin should disable "slug" when page bundles are activated
description: Hi @yihui, I started using the page bundles option recently and noticed an annoying issue with links generated if the New Post Addin works "as usual" and this option is set in your .Rprofile. If you use this option, the default Addin behavior is to populate the post "slug" for you- you cannot *NOT* have a post slug. But, if you *do* use a slug on a bundled post, what populates into your public directory is this: ``` public/ |- 2019-02-20-slug |- slug |- index.html ``` This means that links to your bundled posts (if there is a slug) will double up 😢 . I added [redirects](https://github.com/rbind/apreshill/blob/master/static/_redirects) to fix my two instances of it, but originally the link to a single post looked like this: https://alison.rbind.io/post/2019-02-19-hugo-netlify-toml/hugo-netlify-toml/ And if I tried this link of course it produced a page not found error (since the index file was in a folder): https://alison.rbind.io/post/2019-02-19-hugo-netlify-toml/ But when I removed the slug from the post, the link is correct: https://alison.rbind.io/post/2019-02-19-hugo-netlify-toml/ So I am wondering if the default behavior of the Addin can be changed so that when you have the page bundle option turned on, the slug is deactivated somehow so the user cannot set it? Maybe grayed out? Thanks for considering, Alison see issue #351

title: kable produces malformed reference links after HTML calls in blogdown
description:
This is a replicate of yihui/knitr#1669 but it should be easier to digest since I created a repo to reproduce the issue.

In [this](https://github.com/oganm/bgtest) blogdown repository there is [a post](https://github.com/oganm/bgtest/blob/master/content/post/2019-02-06-test.rmd) which includes a few tables. The repository is created upon running `blogdown::new_site()` and the test post is created by doing `blogdown::new_post("test", ext = ".rmd")`. No other files have been modified in any way. The contents of the file are as follows:

    ---
    title: test
    author: ~
    date: '2019-02-06'
    slug: test
    categories: []
    tags: []
    ---
    
    
    ```{r setup, include=FALSE}
    knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE)
    ```
    
    ```{r test1}
    library(knitr)
    library(magrittr)
    library(kableExtra)
    library(shiny)
    data.frame(a= c(1,2,3)) %>% kable(caption = 'test',format = 'html')
    ```
    
    ```{r test2}
    lapply(1:2,function(x){
        data.frame(a= c(1,2,3)) %>% kable(caption = 'test2',format = 'html') %>% HTML()
    }) -> tables
    tables[[1]]
    tables[[2]]
    ```
    
    
    ```{r test3}
    for(i in 1){
      table = data.frame(a= c(1,2,3)) %>% kable(caption = 'test3',format = 'html') %>% HTML()
    }
    table
    ```
    
    ```{r test4}
    {data.frame(a= c(1,2,3)) %>% kable(caption = 'test4',format = 'html') %>% HTML()}
    ```

And this is how blogdown renders this post

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6352379/52385703-a0bfc100-2a37-11e9-9e00-e974958c5541.png)

The main problem is that whenever kable is in a `{` block the reference tag is created in a wrong way making it visible to the reader of the post in the form of `(\#tag:codeBlockLabel)`.

A lesser problem is that the first table with the proper reference tag is named `Table 1: test` instead of just `test` without my consent.

I want to understand why kable is behaving differently in different contexts within the same file and I want to know how I can control this behaviour ideally getting rid of any helpful attempts by kable to reformat my captions

title: Documentation for syntax highlighting in Rmd posts
description:
Thanks for this project and the great documentation! I recently worked through the blogdown book and built my first website. I wanted to suggest an improvement to the documentation regarding syntax highlighting in Rmd posts that I think would be helpful for new blogdown users. A stumbling point was that I knew `knitr` has built in syntax highlighting, but it doesn't seem to work by default in blogdown Rmd posts. Eventually I figured out that it wasn't on by default in the blogdown::html_page doc type and could be turned on in the Yaml header of the post, 
```
output:
  blogdown::html_page:
    highlight: tango
```
But [discussion of syntax highlighting in the book](https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/templates.html#how-to) doesn't mention this and instead suggests that `highlight.js` and template customization is needed. It isn't really clear if Rmd or plain md posts are being considered there, but in other parts of the book Rmd posts are recommended and the distinctions between md and Rmd posts are clearly made. I think it could be very helpful to clarify in the docs/book that syntax highlighting can be turned on in Rmd posts and (if I'm understanding correctly) that the highlight.js and template-modding is only needed for code not in Rmd r-chunks.

Perhaps it is only with recent versions of blogdown / Hugo that this is possible? The theme I'm using is https://github.com/ribice/kiss which as far as I can tell does not include highlight.js but maybe has some other syntax highlighting support built in.

title: Hugo version 0.53 restructures `config.toml` --> exampleSite won't render
description:
Hi @yihui,

Someone else alerted me to a refactoring of Hugo exampleSites, as with the hugo-academic theme. I reproduced the issue with Hugo version 0.53 using `gcushen/hugo-academic` theme. 

Here is the author's [commit that changed the structure](https://github.com/gcushen/hugo-academic/commit/ae8a86a04794ce5489b9686957045ef1f70ac859).

And here is the new `exampleSite`:
https://github.com/gcushen/hugo-academic/tree/master/exampleSite

The most significant change is that multiple `.toml` files now exist (`languages`, `params`, and `menus` are pulled out separately), instead of one `config.toml` file. 

For reference, here was the old `exampleSite` `config.toml` file:
https://github.com/rbind/apreshill/blob/master/themes/hugo-academic/exampleSite/config.toml

Here is the beginning of the OLD main menus:
```
# Navigation Links
#   To link a homepage widget, specify the URL as a hash `#` followed by the filename of the
#     desired widget in your `content/home/` folder.
#   The weight parameter defines the order that the links will appear in.
[params.menus]
  # Align the main menu to the right of the page? (true/false)
  align_right = true

[[menu.main]]
  name = "Home"
  url = "#about"
  weight = 1
```

In the new `exampleSite` `menu.toml` this same section looks like this:
```
# Navigation Links
#   To link a homepage widget, specify the URL as a hash `#` followed by the filename of the
#     desired widget in your `content/home/` folder.
#   The weight parameter defines the order that the links will appear in.

[[main]]
  name = "Home"
  url = "#about"
weight = 1
```

However, no naive quick fixes worked me (I tried created a master `config.toml` file by pasting the multiples into one and updating the names of the params, I also tried using the old example config file and just pasting that in). Not sure if you have seen this recently with any other themes, but it seemed like a pretty drastic restructuring so wanted to make sure you are aware of it.

title: Support initializing a new_post() with a page bundle
description:
Hi @yihui, after looking through [Romain's question](https://twitter.com/dvaughan32/status/1076857852856332288) on Twitter, I found that [page bundles](https://gohugo.io/content-management/page-bundles/) solve the issue of keeping images and data files separate from the post that they go with. It also plays nicely with RStudio's built in autocomplete and image preview feature, as demonstrated on twitter.

I tried my hand at creating a simple blog using page bundles, which worked nicely here
https://github.com/DavisVaughan/leafblog

After seeing how well it worked, I converted my site to use them. I'm very happy with the result.
https://github.com/DavisVaughan/data-insights/tree/master/content/post


Would it be possible to give `new_post()` a way to init a post with a page bundle setup? It would:

- Create a folder under `post/` with the name that normally is given to the `md`/`Rmd`.
- Create an `index.md` / `index.Rmd` inside that folder

That would be a great resource, at least to me as I try and switch over to using this setup.

The only thing I have had to change after using this setup is the fact that links now look like `base_url/post/2018-01-01-folder-name/slug` which I fixed by setting the `[permalinks]` config parameter to use `post = "/:year/:month/:day/:slug/"`. If users want the exact default behavior, then I think they can use `post = "/post/:slug/"`

* `list_rmds`
* `build_rmds`

title: Enhancement: Use file hashes to determine which Rmd files to knit
description:
I have a site that programmatically generates Rmd files from a database (I use it for teaching, and it does this to automatically update homework assignments, post answers, etc., using the database to automate moving a syllabus from one semester to the next and cross-referencing between assignments).

Because I regenerate .Rmd files, using timestamps to determine what needs to be knit doesn't work. I wrote a small script that I use that hashes source and output files (using `blogdown:::list_rmds()` and `blogdown:::output_file()` to get source and output files, respectively) and maintains a tibble of filenames and hashes in an `.Rds` file in the project root directory.

If this would be of interest to the blogdown maintainers, I could create a PR from this.

```r
needs_rebuild <- function(current_digest, current_dest_digest,
                          old_digest, old_dest_digest) {
     current_digest != old_digest | current_dest_digest != old_dest_digest %>% 
     replace_na(TRUE)
}

digest_if_exists <- function(file) {
  # SHA256 is extreme overkill. CRC32 would be fine.
  # But it takes almost no time to hash a semester's worth of 
  # files.
  if (file.exists(file)) digest(file, file = TRUE, algo = "sha256")
  else as.character(NA)
}

files_to_rebuild <- function(files) {
  base <- here::here()
  files <- unique(files) %>% keep(file.exists)
  df <- tibble(file = files, dest = blogdown:::output_file(files)) %>%
    mutate(cur_digest = map_chr(file, digest_if_exists),
           cur_dest_digest = map_chr(dest, digest_if_exists))

  digest_file <- here::here("digests.Rds")

  if (file.exists(digest_file)) {
    # message("reading digest file")
    digest <- read_rds(digest_file) %>%
      mutate(file = str_replace_all(file, ("^~"), base)) %>%
      select(-dest)
    df <- df %>% left_join(digest, by = "file")
  } else {
    # message("no digest file")
    df <- df %>% mutate(digest = NA, dest_digest = NA)
  }

  df <- df %>%
    mutate(rebuild = needs_rebuild(cur_digest, cur_dest_digest,
                                   digest, dest_digest))

  # For debugging
  # g_files <<- df

  df %>% filter(rebuild) %$% file
}

update_rmd_digests <- function(files) {
  base <- here::here()
  digest_file <- here::here("digests.Rds")
  files <- unique(files) %>% keep(file.exists)
  digests <- tibble(file = files, dest = blogdown:::output_file(files)) %>%
    mutate(digest = map_chr(file, ~digest(.x, file = TRUE, algo = "sha256")),
           dest_digest = map_chr(dest, digest_if_exists),
           file = str_replace_all(file, fixed(base), "~"),
           dest = str_replace_all(dest, fixed(base), "~"))
  write_rds(digests, digest_file)
}

update_site <- function(dir = here::here("content"), quiet = FALSE) {
  files <- blogdown:::list_rmds(dir)
  to_build <- files_to_rebuild(files)
  if (! quiet) {
    message("Building ", length(to_build), " out of date ",
            ifelse(length(to_build) == 1, "file", "files"),
            "; site has ", length(files), " ",
            ifelse(length(files) == 1, "file", "files"),
            " in total.")
  }
  blogdown:::build_rmds(to_build)
  update_rmd_digests(files)
}
```

title: Broken links in RSS feed
description:
When the baseurl of a project is a subdirectory, blogdown can fail to generate the correct image links in the RSS feed. This applies to figures generated by code chunks. 

Steps to reproduce:

## Start a new project 
```r
blogdown::new_site(serve = FALSE)
```

## Edit config.toml

```
baseurl = "https://example.github.io/blog"
```

## Enable full content xml feeds 

Add the hugo embedded [rss.xml](https://gohugo.io/templates/rss/#the-embedded-rss-xml) to layouts/rss.xml then edit L22 to

```
 <description>{{ .Content | html }}</description>
```

## Serve the site

```r
blogdown::serve_site()
```

## View the results 

Navigate to:

http://127.0.0.1:4321/blog/2015/07/23/hello-r-markdown/  (or whichever port you use)

to see the figure generated properly. 

Then navigate to:

http://127.0.0.1:4321/blog/index.xml

and observe that the figure isn't in the full content xml. In the html output approx L102

/blog/blogpost/2015-07-23-r-rmarkdown_files/figure-html/pie-1.png 

does not exist. The redundant /blog comes from the baseurl.

title: Multilingual support in "New post" RStudio addin
description:
One nice thing about Hugo is support for multilingual sites. With a theme making use of this feature, one can specify the language of a post very simply in the file name: `2018-08-10-my-new-post.md` will be assigned the default language by Hugo, while `2018-08-10-my-new-post.<langcode>.md` will be assigned the correct language corresponding to the 2-letter `<langcode>`, and Hugo will place the corresponding html page in `<baseURL>/<langcode>/...` when it builds the site.

Now, when writing a new post I almost always forget to specify the language code in the file name, notice it when previewing the site locally, and fix it. I feel like I would not forget it as easily if the "New post" addin in RStudio had a dropdown menu with available languages (and would construct the filename accordingly for me, just like it already does with the date).
A reasonable default for this menu would be the value of `defaultContentLanguage` in `config.toml`, and the menu could auto-detect other language codes in use in already existing files (just like existing tags and categories are detected by the addin). Or alternatively, make it "smart" and default to the most commonly used language code based on already existing posts? Could be nice too.

Any chance this little feature could be added to the "New post" addin? If so, that would be great. 😃

title: Starting with version 2.2.0 hugo-academic does not work with RMarkdown/blogdown anymore
description:
After updating blogdown and the hugo academic theme I noticed after a while that with `"Build" -> "More…" -> "Clean All" blogdown:::serve_site()` blogdown did not produce a preview of the website but created the index of the site. I have reported all the details with error messages, sessionInfo etc. at the [forum of the RStudio Community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/serve-site-creates-index-of-site-rather-than-site-preview-blogdown/11120).

At first it was difficult to provide a reproducible example with my website but then I noticed that a new installation with blogdown & the academic theme produced this error immediately after installation with the first `serve_site()`.

I started the rollback to previous version with blogdown but this didn't help. So it appears that your package blogdown is not the cause. Finally it turned out that with version 2.2.0 of the academic theme this error emerged. I reported it to @gcushen but he thinks that the problems must be in blogdown.

> ... it appears unrelated to the Academic code. Academic works fine when used directly with Hugo. Since the problem only occurs with Blogdown and based on your comments and the fact that Blogdown acts as a wrapper around Hugo, it would appear that there may be a bug in Blogdown.

Frankly speaking, I do not know where the problem could be. I am a little surprised (and worried) that I am the first user to notice this problem as I know many people are using your blogdown package with the academic theme. A possible explanation may be that not so many people did recently update and – more important – the error does only appear in a working website after you are using the menue button "Build" -> "More…" -> "Clean All". As this is not a common procedure, so maybe this is the reason that people have not yet noticed this problem.

```
bases = with_ext(files, '')
files = files[!i & bases == bases[i]]  # files with same basename as f (Rmd)
if (length(files) == 0 || any(older_than(files, f))) render_it()
```

It just so happens, in my case, that my blog post folders (coming from Jekyll) are named like `2018-06-28-cool-project`, with both the Rmd and Rproj file always using the same basename (`2018-06-28-cool-project.Rmd`, `2018-06-28-cool-project.Rproj`). I don't remember where I picked up this convention, but in any case, it succesfully manages to trick the `older_than` check to always detect an older "output" file, since (in this case) the Rproj file is indeed older and always shares the same basename with the Rmd file. 

A simple demonstration:
```
> files
[1] "/hugo/content/post/2018-06-28-cool-project/2018-06-28-cool-project.html" 
[2] "/hugo/content/post/2018-06-28-cool-project/2018-06-28-cool-project.Rproj"
> f 
"/hugo/content/post/2018-06-28-cool-project/2018-06-28-cool-project.Rmd"
> blogdown:::older_than(files, f)
[1] FALSE  TRUE
```
Which naturally causes `any(older_than(files, f))` to always return `TRUE`.

This causes much longer rebuilds than necessary (although I must say the Hugo step really is a bullet train compared to Jekyll's horsecart!).

A simple solution for me would be to just change the names of my Rproj files to something other than the basename of my Rmd files. But I thought perhaps this situation might affect others and warrant a different approach?

title: Bug: Don't build draft RMD's
description:
# Problem

While there are performance considerations to not building 'draft' Rmd's, the larger and more pressing issue is that all build documents have their by-products (images, etc) get copied so even though hugo won't build pages for drafts, all the images are still made and placed in the built site.

# Proposal

In `build_site`, when local = FALSE, add a step to filter out files where draft is true (or corresponding `blogdown.draft.output` setting) 

I'm happy to perform the coding and create a pull request if this is acceptable.

title: Feature Proposal: Default Rmd to draft
description:
## Feature overview

Add a configuration parameter (`blogdown.draftDefault`) to make Rmd's render out as drafts unless explicitly overridden in their frontmatter.

## Usecase

For more complex analysis, I use a dedicated git repository, with a typical project folder structure - e.g. data, posts, scripts, etc. To add posts from these, I add them as git submodules to my site. The trouble is that I often have non-post Rmd files I don't want rendered to the site - Articles, Presentations, Introductions for collaborators, status reports, etc.

I'd like to be able to easily not include Rmd's not intended as posts (or sharing).

## Alternatives

 * Manually adding 'draft: true' to all Rmd's - besides being more work, this poses the risk of missing a file and having it published without being intended.
 * Making a change to hugo - I think this use case is specific enough to analysis that is is appropriate to add here.
 * Clever use of hugo ignoreFiles - frankly I can't quite think of how to make this work, but there might be something doable...

## Implementation

I'd suggest adding the logic to 'prepend_yaml'. I'm happy to do the work and submit a pull request, but wanted to make sure it was a reasonable proposal before doing the work.

title: TOC generation is different in blogdown from Hugo's default via blackfriday
description:
When the markdown files are parsed by Blackfriday, then Hugo apparently automatically generates IDs for heading elements. As mentioned [in this thread](https://discourse.gohugo.io/t/hugo-is-generating-css-ids-for-heading-elements-should-it/3284/2), they are:

> used for lots of cool stuff, anchor identities for the autogenerated table of contents, to give one example.

Blogdown appears to have it's own toc generation mechanism, but I believe that uses wrapper div classes with IDs attached to them. This seems to be a small difference between the way markdown is rendered by blackfriday v/s the default blogdown way.

I'm raising this issue to suggest that it may be a good idea to mention this in the [documentation](https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/) in the chapter explaining the [differences between RMarkdown and Markdown](https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/output-format.html).

I realize it's not a big deal, but it took me a while to figure out what was up with the TOC of my Hugo theme ([Er](https://github.com/lingxz/er)) not working - because it was relying on the h1 classes being generated in a particular way. I don't think blogdown needs to change in anyway, just a heads up in the documentation would be helpful. [In my situation](http://blog.neeldhara.com/post/2018/june/firstdjangoapp/), I simply turned off Er's TOC and switched to blogdown's. 

Thanks for considering this!

I have been attempting to set up a personal website using RStudio, the [blogdown](https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown) package, the [Academic](https://github.com/gcushen/hugo-academic) theme and the blogdown "Serve Site" RStudio addin.

I know next to nothing about all this and have been following the instructions in Alison Presmanes Hill's [blog](https://alison.rbind.io/post/up-and-running-with-blogdown/) and the [blogdown](https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/) book.

Everything was going well, i.e. when I made and saved changes to the text of contents, the serve site addin would detect the change and locally re-render the site. (This is all local to my development PC. I haven't attempted to deploy via Netlify yet.)

Then I tried to enable permalinks for posts, as [suggested in the blogdown book](https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/configuration.html#options). This was done by adding the following text somewhere near the top of `config.toml`.
```
    [permalinks]
        post = "/:year/:month/:day/:slug/"
```
After adding those lines the site would not re-render. That is, if I changed any text in the content files the rendered output did not pick up the changes. There were no error messages in the RStudio console.

I filed this on what appeared to be a [related issue in hugo-academic](https://github.com/gcushen/hugo-academic/issues/534), but the owner was unable to replicate this as a purely hugo/academic issue.

> @rgayler I have set [permalinks] for all 4 types of content in a test
> environment with the example site, running latest versions of Hugo and
> Academic and cannot reproduce the issue which you have described.
> Hence, based on the details which you have provided, it may possibly
> be a bug relating to Blogdown/Rstudio.

In another reply to someone else about permalink problems from blogdown the hugo-academic owner also suggested that this (other, possibly related) problem was only arising for blogdown users - so was possibly a blogdown issue.

> @jananiravi it appears that this issue is only affecting
> Blogdown/RStudio users and may be related to Blogdown/RStudio
> compatibility with Hugo's permalinks and GetPage functionality.

I have created a minimal example. Unfortunately, it's two snapshots (commits) of an [entire website as generated by blogdown](https://github.com/rgayler/blogdown_reprex/commits/master). The 6th commit (SHA = cc0f2cb) shows the website while it is working. It corresponds to the Academic example installed following the [instructions](https://alison.rbind.io/post/up-and-running-with-blogdown/). The 7th commit (SHA = 2b0eefa) shows the website after adding and saving the permalink lines to `config.toml`, then changing and saving the header text of `about.md`. This change does not get rendered.

Any clues as to what is happening here would be greatly appreciated. For the moment I am working around this by doing without permalinks.

title: Custom Output Format for Content
description:
Hi Yihui,

I want to use a custom output format when rendering posts in blogdown. In particular, I want to use the tufte output format `tufte::tufte_html` when rendering blogposts. I'm aware that blogdown renders .Rmd files with `blogdown::html_page`, I can see this in the `render_page` script. 

```r
out = rmarkdown::render(
    input, 'blogdown::html_page', envir = globalenv(), quiet = TRUE,
    encoding = 'UTF-8', run_pandoc = !to_md, clean = !to_md
)
``` 

I'm also aware that to render arbitrary .Rmd files we can specify a `build.R` file to render them using the arguments in the YAML front matter, however this only seems to work when building files under the `static` directory. When setting `build.R` to `blogdown::build_dir('content')` blog posts are not rendered using `tufte::tufte_html` as specified in it's front matter. 

I assume it is a design choice that posts are only rendered by `blogdown::html_page`. Is it possible to specify the output format of a post in `content/post/` in blogdown currently? 

Otherwise I think this feature could be implemented by simply passing the specified YAML arguments to `rmarkdown::render`. Could I help with this feature?

Thanks,
Dan

title: anyone prefer to refresh serve_site manually?
description:
The auto refresh of `serve_site` is supposed to be reduce user's effort and see changes immediately. However I met these problems:
- With `serve_site` on, the file browser in RStudio is very slow. Every folder change take about 2 seconds.
- It often take a long time to save a file.
- If site rendering met some problem, the next refresh is scheduled by a wait time, and it will increase by each failure. This could mean I need to wait half minute if I took 2 attempts to fix the problem.

A manual refresh will work for me and avoid all the problems above. I'm wondering if there is more users feel this way.

I looked at the code about the possible changes:
- We can add a `auto_fresh = TRUE` parameter and still use live preview as default
- For manual refresh, maybe we just need to call `serve_it` again without using `servr:::watch_dir`?
 I'm not totally sure about the best approach here.
- Once we have a function to refresh the site, we can have a rstudio addin and bind some keyboard shortcut.

title: Insert external image addin
description: Hi Yihui, I was about write an updated version of http://lcolladotor.github.io/2018/02/17/r-markdown-blog-template using the new changes from https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/pull/263. I then realized that inserting external (non R images) takes enough work that it might scare off some users. This has been discussed in https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/239. I know that another option is to use `knitr::insert_graphics()` but then the user has to organize the pictures someway that avoids creating files at `blogpath/content/post`. So I made an addin for inserting pictures that copies the selected file to `blogpath/static/postdir/` and inserts the HTML code for showing a picture. I chose HTML since that should work with .md, .Rmd and .Rmarkdown blog posts + gives control on the width/height. What's the best option for submitting a PR? Should I delete my first fork at https://github.com/lcolladotor/blogdown and remake one? Some of the solutions at https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28119733/how-can-i-make-a-second-fork-of-a-github-project (a new account, forking to an organization) don't seem like the best to me. ## Addin demo Select addin from the addins menu If the user didn't have a file selected (for example they had the console selected), end in an error with a useful message. Addin after filling some options Text is inserted, console prints the location of where the image was copied to. Useful if new users want to learn what is going on. ## Addin code Contents of `inst/scripts/insert_image.R`. It's based on `inst/scripts/new_post.R` ```R local({ txt_input = function(..., width = '100%') shiny::textInput(..., width = width) blogfile = rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext() if(blogfile$path == '') stop('Please select the blog post source file before using this addin', call. = FALSE) imgdir = file.path( gsub('/content/.*', '', normalizePath(blogfile$path)), 'static', dirname(gsub('.*content/', '', normalizePath(blogfile$path))), paste0(xfun::sans_ext(basename(blogfile$path)), '_files') ) shiny::runGadget( miniUI::miniPage(miniUI::miniContentPanel( shiny::fillRow( shiny::fileInput('newimg', 'Image', placeholder = 'Select external image'), height = '100px' ), shiny::fillRow( txt_input('imgwidth', 'Image width', '', '(optional) Example: 400 for 400px'), txt_input('imgheight', 'Image height', '', '(optional) Example: 200 for 200px'), height = '70px'), shiny::fillRow( txt_input('imgalt', 'Image alternative text', '', '(optional) Example: awesome screenshot'), height = '70px' ), miniUI::gadgetTitleBar(NULL) )), server = function(input, output, session) { shiny::observeEvent(input$done, { if (is.null(input$newimg)) return( warning('You have to choose an image!', call. = FALSE) ) dir.create(imgdir, showWarnings = FALSE) file.copy(input$newimg$datapath, file.path(imgdir, input$newimg$name)) if(file.exists(file.path(imgdir, input$newimg$name))) message(paste('successfully copied the image to', file.path(imgdir, input$newimg$name))) imgsrc = paste0( "/", basename(dirname(imgdir)), "/", basename(imgdir), "/", input$newimg$name ) image_text = if(input$imgwidth == '' & input$imgheight == '') shiny::img(src = imgsrc) else if (input$imgwidth == '') shiny::img(src = imgsrc, height = input$imgheight) else if(input$imgheight == '') shiny::img(src = imgsrc, width = input$imgwidth) else shiny::img(src = imgsrc, width = input$imgwidth, height = input$imgheight) rstudioapi::insertText(as.character(image_text)) shiny::stopApp() }) shiny::observeEvent(input$cancel, { shiny::stopApp() }) }, stopOnCancel = FALSE, viewer = shiny::dialogViewer('Add external image to a blogdown post', height = 270) ) }) ``` Changes to `R/utils.R` (around line 325) ```R insert_image_addin = function() { sys.source(pkg_file('scripts', 'insert_image.R')) } ``` Changes at the end of `inst/rstudio/addins.dcf` ``` Name: Insert image Description: Insert an external image into a blogdown post Binding: insert_image_addin Interactive: true ``` Best, Leo

title: new_post() when using `kind` and `ext` only works with .md extensions for both the archetype and the blog post
description: Hi again, I noticed that `new_post()` works with a supplied `kind` argument only when `ext = '.md'` and not when `ext = '.Rmd'`. Also, the `kind` template has to end in `.md` even if the `ext = '.Rmd'`. This could be related to https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/173#issuecomment-367888459 and is ultimately related to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48844340/is-it-possible-to-create-a-rmd-file-template-for-the-blogdown-new-post-addin. I'm posting this here because I'm not sure that the current behaviour is the intended one. In any case, it can lead to some confusion as to why it appears that `blogdown` is not using a specified archetype (say `archetypes/default.md`) when using a `ext` value different from `'.md'`. Also, even in the case that it works (`.md` extension for the archetype and `ext = '.md'`) the user still needs to change the file extension manually of the new post file if they wanted to use `.Rmd` or `.Rmarkdown`. Plus add any YAML lines exclusive to `.Rmd` that are not used in `.md`. Things work, just not in all cases. From https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/a079068000fe86512503454f28dee49b486b3057/R/hugo.R#L193 and https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/a079068000fe86512503454f28dee49b486b3057/R/hugo.R#L7 this looks like it's outside the real of `blogdown`. Though maybe `blogdown` could internally replace the archetypes that end with non `.md` terminations so that they use that termination (or just show an error telling the user to use a `.md` archetype), and then switch the new blog post file termination from `.md` to whatever was supposed the user wanted. I'm not 100% sure that `new_post()` https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/a079068000fe86512503454f28dee49b486b3057/R/hugo.R#L273-L276 then adds the YAML that is only used in `.Rmd` blog posts. I'm referring to parts like this: ``` output: blogdown::html_page: toc: no fig_width: 5 fig_height: 5 ``` Thanks again for the great package and tools! Best, Leo ## Tests Using the `hugo-academic` `posts.md` archetype, I created two identical files `archetypes/posts.md` and `archetypes/jojo.Rmd` (the main difference is that one has a `.md` file termination and the other one `.Rmd`) where I added some extra R markdown code from [here](http://lcolladotor.github.io/2018/02/17/r-markdown-blog-template/). I then ran several tests where I use each archetype twice, once with `ext = '.md'` and one with `ext = '.Rmd'`. The case that works well is when I use `posts.md` with `ext = '.md'`. ```R > blogdown::new_post('hola7', kind = 'posts.md', slug = 'hola', ext = '.Rmd') /Users/lcollado/Dropbox/Code/hugoblog/content/post/2018-02-22-hola7.Rmd created [1] "content/post/2018-02-22-hola7.Rmd" > blogdown::new_post('hola8', kind = 'posts.md', slug = 'hola', ext = '.md') /Users/lcollado/Dropbox/Code/hugoblog/content/post/2018-02-22-hola8.md created [1] "content/post/2018-02-22-hola8.md" > blogdown::new_post('hola9', kind = 'jojo.Rmd', slug = 'hola', ext = '.Rmd') /Users/lcollado/Dropbox/Code/hugoblog/content/post/2018-02-22-hola9.Rmd created [1] "content/post/2018-02-22-hola9.Rmd" > blogdown::new_post('hola10', kind = 'jojo.Rmd', slug = 'hola', ext = '.md') /Users/lcollado/Dropbox/Code/hugoblog/content/post/2018-02-22-hola10.md created processing 4 content files [1] "content/post/2018-02-22-hola10.md" > dir('archetypes') [1] "default.md" "jojo.Rmd" "posts.md" ``` It took me a bit longer to diagnose this issue because I have in my `.Rprofile` two options set to help reduce time when using the RStudio addin. ```R options(blogdown.author = 'L. Collado-Torres') options(blogdown.ext = '.Rmd') ``` ## Screenshots Here I include screenshots that show how the `hola7`, `hola8` and `hola9` test fail but the `hola8` works. #### hola7 test: posts.md with .Rmd #### hola8 test: posts.md with .md Yay, this worked! Well, almost. The file ends with `.md` and not `.Rmd` so I'd have to manually change the file extension. #### hola9 test: jojo.Rmd with .Rmd #### hola10 test: jojo.Rmd with .md This actually generates a slightly different YAML by including ``` header: caption: '' image: '' ``` ## `archetypes/posts.md` content ``` +++ title = "{{ replace .TranslationBaseName "-" " " | title }}" date = {{ .Date }} draft = false # Tags and categories # For example, use `tags = []` for no tags, or the form `tags = ["A Tag", "Another Tag"]` for one or more tags. tags = [] categories = [] # Featured image # Place your image in the `static/img/` folder and reference its filename below, e.g. `image = "example.jpg"`. [header] image = "" caption = "" +++ ## Doesn't really have the next + sign, but just so I could show some edits I made + ```{r bibsetup, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} ## Load knitcitations with a clean bibliography library('knitcitations') cleanbib() cite_options(hyperlink = 'to.doc', citation_format = 'text', style = 'html') bib <- c('knitcitations' = citation('knitcitations'), 'blogdown' = citation('blogdown')[2]) +``` ``` ## R session info Same as in https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/173#issuecomment-367888459

title: Blogdown setting incorrect fig.path for knitr chunks
description:
# Simple description

`build_site()` sets knitr `fig.path` to `*_files/figure-html4/` instead of `*_files/figure-html/` and this causes blogdown to move figure files to the wrong destination within the `static` directory.

# Minimal reproducible example

1. I create a new blogdown web site project from RStudio.
1. I build the default site, as blogdown creates it.
1. The "pie-1.png" figure ends up in `static/rmarkdown-libs/figure-html4/pie-1.png` instead of `static/post/2015-07-23-r-markdown_files/figure-html/pie-1.png`.

## Further info:

* I use the RStudio blogdown add-in to create a new `.Rmd` post and make a code chunk called `pie`, which creates a figure. When I build the site, there is a collision between the two posts writing different `pie-1.png` files to the same path `static/rmarkdown-libs/figure-html4/pie-1.png`

* If I edit the `setup` chunk of the default post to be:
    ```
    {r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE}
    knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE)

    message("Dep path = ", blogdown::dep_path())
    message("fig.path = ", knitr::opts_chunk$get("fig.path"))
    ```
    then the output is
    ```
    Dep path = 2015-07-23-r-rmarkdown_files/figure-html4/setup
    fig.path = 2015-07-23-r-rmarkdown_files/figure-html4/
    ```
   From the documentation, the path should end with `figure-html/`, not `figure-html4`,

title: Complicated math expressions not rendered
description:
I am still having difficulties with math expressions in Hugo and blogdown.
It works for simple equations, but more complicated ones are not rendered.

I am trying to achieve this:

$$\prod_{c = 1}^{k} (l_c + 1) = 1 + \sum_{c = 1}^{k}\binom{k}{c}\prod_{s = 1}^{c} l_s$$

$$\prod_{c = 1}^{k} (l_c + 1)$$
or
$$\sum_{c = 1}^{k} \binom{k}{c}$$

but not with
$$\sum_{c = 1}^{k}\binom{k}{c}\prod_{s = 1}^{c} l_s$$
(and neither with the entire equation).

Any hints would be greatly appreciated. Using the latest version of blogdown, and version 0.36 of Hugo.

title: Resize image in static directory
description:
I am trying to resize an image in the static directory.

I am trying to resize an image, in particular one in the `static/_media/` directory.

For example, on [a page on my Hugo site](https://jrosen48.github.io/teaching/), I added the following two lines to the top of the `.md` file:

    ![test image](/_media/logos/pdf_100100.png)
    
    ![test image 2](/_media/logos/pdf.png)

The first is resized to have dimensions of 100 x 100 pixels, while the second is 720 x 720. However, they both render the same size. How can I resize an image - either outside of or within Blogdown?

Note: I asked two related questions on Stack Overflow on the topic ([here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48139980/resize-image-on-hugo-site-generated-with-blogdown?noredirect=1#comment83263672_48139980), [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48063067/resize-image-in-hugo-v-0-32)), and the consensus seems to be that you cannot resize them without the use of shortcodes. Separate from the issue of how to *resize* an image, I'm confused why images with different dimensions appear as the same size, as the two images on the page linked above are. Thank you for any help!

title: Blogdown book suggestions related to updating
description:
I do not (yet) use blogdown but I keep thinking that it might be the best way for me to manage a Hugo site. Periodically I fire up RStudio, which I installed in 2017 when I first experimented with Blogdown, and hit these stumbling blocks:

* How do I update R?
* How do I update RStudio?
* How do I update Blogdown?

In August, I figured out how to update Hugo from within RStudio, thanks to the
[blogdown book](https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/), and I posted issue https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/issues/179 suggesting that the book have a separate section about updating. Thank you for creating section **1.1.1 Update**. I have another suggestion: Please discuss or give links in the book about how to update R, RStudio, and blogdown. My guess is that most of your audience knows this, but some of us have zero experience with R and RStudio and don't know these basic things. It would be useful to have this info in the book so I don't have to go off on a web search to learn these things.

In case you're wondering why I want to use R and RStudio considering that I know nothing about them, it's because 1) blogdown seems cool and 2) I'm a math nerd and have dreams of including graphs and fractals and other math nerdery in a Hugo blog.

description:

title: Possible bug parsing a `config.toml` which contains inline comments
description:
Say we have a `config.toml` where the first line contains a comment after the variable:
```
baseurl = "/"  # End your URL with a `/` trailing slash, e.g. `https://example.com/`.
```
This is valid TOML and works fine in Hugo (as expected), however, when using the Blogdown wrapper, an error appears complaining about the `#` symbol. I have not had time to fully investigate the root cause, but it would appear that it is a bug relating to Blogdown not correctly parsing the `baseurl` TOML.

Blogdown reports in Console:
```
Serving the directory test at http://127.0.0.1:4321/"/"  # End your URL with a `/` trailing slash, e.g. `https://example.com/`.
```

Blogdown reports in Viewer:
```
Not found:
./"/"  
```

The error can be produced with the latest public release of Blogdown, Hugo v0.30.2, and the latest version of Academic theme (gcushen/hugo-academic).

title: Add more bibliography entries and an index

These entries are automatically generated in https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/blob/master/docs/10-references.Rmd I'm not sure if there are any other publications to be cited.

1. An index. You can take a look at the Rmd source files of the bookdown book, in which you may occasionally find `\index{}`. That is how you add index entries. This only works for PDF output. Watch out for special characters such as underscores -- they may need to be escaped by backslashes. See the last page of the bookdown book for an example: https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/bookdown.pdf

The readme file has explained how to compile the book to PDF: https://github.com/rstudio/blogdown/tree/master/docs

title: Weird issue with crashing chrome tab
description:
First off, thank you for this awesome package!

I had a really weird issue (fixed) but I think it may point to a bug somewhere. 

I have been running the blog http://www.statsathome.com/ for a few months without problems. I recently wrote a post http://www.statsathome.com/2017/09/14/visualizing-the-multinomial-in-the-simplex/. (github rmarkdown here: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsilve24/stats_at_home/master/content/post/2017-09-14-visualizing-the-multinomial-in-the-simplex.Rmd)

At first the page would render fine in the Rstudio browser and on safari but it would crash if I tried to open it in a chrome tab. Ultimately I ended up having to rewrite a few lines (not actually changing anything of note) and I eventually got it to work. 

It did not occur if Rmarkdown was compiled and that file was opened, only if it was compiled through blogdown and opened as part of my site. 

## How to replicate problem:  
* Download my github repo:  https://github.com/jsilve24/stats_at_home
* in the file content/post/2017-09-14-visualizing-the-multinomial-in-the-simplex.Rmd remove the second call `d <- setNames(as.data.frame(prob), c("v1", "v2", "v3"))` under the heading "Effect of changing $n$ (counting as a random process)" which should be on line 73. Note that this line should not be required as it is called in the block above. 
* Try to serve the site and open this page in chrome. 

I am sorry if this does not work for you, it was reproducible on my machine. Each time I try this it just loads and loads and eventually I get a message asking if I want to kill the tab. As I said, its all fixed for me, but the fix is weird and unintuitive and was very time consuming to figure out. 

## Versions
Using package Version 0.1 for blogdown (installed via CRAN)
Hugo version 0.26

Hopefully this helps squash a bug.
Justin

title: Pre-installed Hugo and install_hugo()
description:
Hi,

I tried gitlab pages a few weeks ago (before discovering blogdown), so I followed their tutorial and installed Hugo from the ubuntu repositories (16.04 actually). Which was hugo 0.19.

Reading your documentation I tried to install Hugo from the R command (silly me) provided by blogdown.
Curiously it works and installed Hugo. But the called version was still the 0.19.

So I remove Hugo 0.19 from the main system, but Hugo wasn't found.

I reused the R command, which reinstalled Hugo. 

But Hugo wasn't found too. 

So I used snap to get a newer version:

```bash
sudo snap install hugo
```
And now I have Hugo 0.26 \o/ and blogdown is pretty well working !!

Not a major issue, but blogdown installed hugo twice but can't use it, which is useless.

I'm posting it to see if an improvement can be made, or at least, show another way for people having the same issue.

I might have forget some informations from the documentation too.

title: blogdown - github - netlify works for md, but not for rmd
description:
First of all: thanks and congrats, blogdown is a fantastic beast that made a guy like me thinking about hosting a website and move slowly into the 21st century.

I worked myself through the blogdown book/documentation with glimpses to some online tutorials, I managed to deploy a first stab (using the bootstrap v4 theme) via netlify (http://rqkoelle.netlify.com).

Adding new pages as md (e.g. about-me) and more blog posts as md files do allow to run the hugo build on netlify. 
However, if i use Rmd to make use of r in a blog this pipeline fails. In fact, the build is successfully completed, but the Rmd files are not converted into payload.
While the files sit nicely in the post/ folder: https://github.com/rainer-rq-koelle/rq-netlify-blog/tree/master/content/post nothing ends up in the public folder that serves the site.

I understand that the build command obviously only uses hugo on netlify and not the magic of blogdown I can use locally. 

Is there a way to achieve this via the netlify deploy as well?
Or can i do something like blogdown::build_post() to just create the desired rmd to html conversion which can then be pushed to github?

My understanding from the first push of the local build_site() is that netlify seems to tolerate the html files created from the rmd in the public folder.
I would just like to avoid having to push loads of files when doing a local build to ensure the rmd to html conversion on a single (or little number of) files.

Thanks.

title: Manipulating plot output (to use lightbox2)
description: I was hoping to include [lightbox2][lightbox] in my blog, because blogposts with multiple generated plots deserve a way to quickly browse through the plots if so desired. Required: - Wrap the plot's `` element in a custom ``-tag with `href` set to the `src` of the `img` - Add `data-lightbox` attributes to the `` tag, also dependent on the plot (title|caption|id) The search for a solution lead me to knitr internals like hooks, which I haven't played around with before, but the result is [this code snippet that I load at the top of each Rmd-blogpost](https://github.com/jemus42/blog.jemu.name/blob/master/global.R): ```r hook <- function(x, options) { width <- height <- '' if (!is.null(options$out.width)) width <- sprintf(' width = "%s" ', options$out.width) if (!is.null(options$out.height)) height <- sprintf(' height = "%s" ', options$out.height) filename <- paste0("../../../post/", knitr::opts_knit$get('base.url'), paste(x, collapse = '.')) if (!is.null(options$fig.cap)) { caption <- paste0("") } else { caption <- NULL } plot_id <- paste0(paste0(sample(c(letters, LETTERS), size = 5, replace = T), collapse = ""), caption) img <- paste0("") lightbox <- paste0("", img, "") figure <- paste0("") return(figure) } knitr::knit_hooks$set(plot = hook) ``` I'm aware this seems crudely hacked together (which is accurate), but the resulting HTML seems fine to me: ```html ``` Which seems to be at least valid. If I check the source of a post generated this way (see link below), the attributes seem to be set correctly and the post itself looks fine, the image is there, it's a hyperlink to itself (which I wanted to add anyway), but a click doesn't trigger lightbox, which saddens me greatly, because I ran out of ideas on how to debug this. I have also tried wrapping the `img` in a `div` instead of a `figure` with the same result. So if anyone has a prettier idea on how to make things like lightbox work (or any idea why it doesn't seem to work in my case), I'd be happy to get some suggestions. References: - [Example blogpost](https://blog.jemu.name/2017/07/prepping-for-winter-kind-of/) - [source for that post](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jemus42/blog.jemu.name/master/content/post/2017-07-17-prepping-for-winter-kind-of.Rmd) - [Blog repo](https://github.com/jemus42/blog.jemu.name) - [My theme](https://github.com/jemus42/hugo-redlounge-jemsu) [lightbox]: http://lokeshdhakar.com/projects/lightbox2/

title: Incorrect URL for img when rendering Rmd file in top level
description:
How to reproduce: create a new Rmd post and set subdirectory to empty so that the Rmd goes into top level of content directory. In the new post add any R chunk that plots something, e.g. ```{r} curve(sin(x), from=-pi, to=+pi) ``` Then serve the site. What happens is that the rendered images are correctly copied into the static directory and also correctly to the toplevel of public directory, but the generated HTML has incorrect URL: 
curve(sin(x), from=-pi, to=+pi)

In particular, the leading `content/` should not be there.

title: Expose a `change_theme` function or :::change_config()
description: Currently the only way (I noticed at first glance) to change configs without diving into `config.toml` is to `blogdown::install_theme()`.  That helpfully has the default of `update_config = TRUE`.  However, if you want to go back and use a previously installed theme, without modifying `config.toml` by hand, it seems like you have to delete the theme directory and run `install_theme()` again.  For ease of use, it seems like an `update_theme()` or exposing `:::change_config()` would be great.  If you agree, but don't want to prioritize this, then I'd be glad to open a PR.

title: Consider RcppTOML for parsing TOML?
description: I'm beginning to work on extending the new post addin as we discussed elsewhere and noticed that the `blogdown:::parse_toml` function is not picking up a lot of the params defined in my theme's archetype files for each type of post.  I just discovered [`RcppTOML`](http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/code/rcpp.toml.html) and it looks like a great solution to deal with potentially complicated `toml` structures.  I realize that `blogdown` and by extension `rmarkdown` don't have `Rcpp` or any extensions of `Rcpp` as dependencies at this time, but as `blogdown` matures it may be worth incorporating `RcppTOML` to bring the parsing of `toml` on near equal footing to the `yaml` parsing that makes heavy use of the `yaml` package.

title: check hashes instead of file timestamps for the rebuild condition?
description:
If I have this right, blogdown applies a `make`-like rule for determining if an `.Rmd` file should be re-run.  Overall I think this is excellent (definitely better than relying on knitr caching, which would be too cumbersome in this case).   However, one thing that's always bothered me about `make` is that timestamps all get messed up by git operations such as changing between branches  in a directory (or when recovering from backups etc).  Seems to make more sense to just keep a quick log of file hashes to decide if a source file has changed more recently than its target (e.g. a la [remake](https://github.com/richfitz/remake) or many other make alternatives), since that would be much less fragile.  Maybe this is a lot more tricky then I'm realizing; and maybe most users won't be so concerned about just when & how their site rebuilds from scratch, but just wanted to bring it up.  

Meanwhile, might also be good to document the rebuild / not rebuild behavior more visibly.

title: header option to ignore an .Rmd file / or ability to recognize alternate output format?
description:
Would it be possible to support an option in the yaml metadata of an .Rmd post which would tell blogdown not to build the file automatically?  

**Rationale**: Sometimes I want .Rmd files in my site repo that have alternative output formats, e.g. a `content/slides` directory that has .Rmd files which already use an `output:` command to specify some slide format (e.g. slides for a lecture).  I can knit these separately, but currently blogdown will compile these .Rmds as if they were regular posts, ignoring the requested output format and overwriting a previously-generated `html`.  It would be simplest and most convenient if blogdown just ignored these .Rmds, and then their original outputs can still be part of the website in unaltered form.  

Alternately, it would be nice if blogdown could recognize requested `output:` formats in yaml and render accordingly via rmarkdown, instead of following the usual knit command.

title: Test sourcetools::read_lines
description:
It is much faster than `readLines()`, and even faster than my hack `blogdown:::readUTF8`:

```r
text <- replicate(10000, {
  paste(sample(letters, 200, TRUE), collapse = "")
})
file <- tempfile()
cat(text, file = file, sep = "\n")
mb <- microbenchmark::microbenchmark(
  times = 10,
  base::readLines(file),
  blogdown:::readUTF8(file),
  sourcetools::read_lines(file)
)
sm <- summary(mb)
print(sm[c("expr", "mean", "median")], digits = 3)
```

```
                           expr  mean median
1         base::readLines(file) 182.9  182.1
2     blogdown:::readUTF8(file)  29.4   28.8
3 sourcetools::read_lines(file)  17.8   15.9
```

Need to make sure the result can be correctly marked as UTF8.
